The great river flows east, its waves washing away all heroes of a thousand years.
On the west side of the old fortress, people say this is where Zhou Yu, general of the Three Kingdoms, made his stand at Red Cliff.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky; roaring tides crash against the shore, churning up heaps of snow-like foam.
The landscape is like a painting—how many heroes gathered in that brief moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime, with Xiao Qiao newly wed, his heroic bearing radiant and bold.
Clad in a silk scarf, holding a feather fan, he laughed and chatted while enemy ships turned to ash and smoke.
Wandering my mind back to that ancient land, surely love-struck hearts would laugh at me, my hair already white.
Life in this world is but a dream—I raise one last cup to offer it to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves sweeping away the romantic heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the ancient ramparts,
They say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu stood in the Three Kingdoms era.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling tides crash against the shore,
Rolling up heaps of snow-like foam.
Mountains and rivers are picturesque as paintings;
How many heroes gathered here in that brief moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic bearing elegant and bold.
With feather fan and silk headscarf,
Amidst laughter and talk,
The enemy fleet dissolved into ash and smoke.
My soul wanders in the ancient land;
Those sentimental souls must laugh at me for my early white hair.
Human life is but a fleeting dream;
I pour this libation to the river moon."}

With feather fan and silk headscarf, while talking and laughing, the enemy's warships were reduced to ash and smoke.
My spirit roams over the ancient kingdom; sentimental as I am, they would laugh at me for growing gray hair too soon.
Human life is like a dream; let me pour a cup of wine to pay respect to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "Great River, Flowing East

The great river flows eastward;
Its waves wash away all the heroic figures of a thousand ages.
To the west lies an old fortress,
said to be Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.
Ragged rocks pierce the sky;
Startling waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The landscape is like a painting;
How many heroes came together in this one moment!

I recall Gongjin from long ago;
Little Qiao had just married him,
His heroic bearing sharp and spirited.
With a feather fan and a silk headscarf,
While laughing and talking casually,
The enemy fleet vanished in ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders back to that ancient kingdom;
If I am too emotional, they might laugh at me,
As my hair has turned white prematurely.
Life on earth is but a dream;
I pour out a libation to the moon reflected in the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves have washed away
The romantic figures of a thousand ages.

West of the old fortress,
Men say, was the Red Cliff of Zhou Lang,
Of the Three Kingdoms.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Surging waves crash on the shore,
Churning up piles of snow.

The rivers and mountains are like a painting;
How many heroes at once!

I think of Gongjin in his prime,
Xiaoqiao newly wed,
His heroic bearing, brilliant and fierce.

With feather fan and silk headband,
In his talk and laughter,
The enemy masts and oars were burned to ash and smoke.

My soul wanders to his ancient land;
If they were sentimental, they would laugh at me,
For my temples have grown white with age.

The human world is like a dream;
Let me pour a cup of wine to the river and moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves have washed away the heroes of a thousand ages.
To the west of the old fortifications, people say, lies Chibi,
Where Zhou Yu, general of the Three Kingdoms, once stood.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky;
Startling waves beat the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
Rivers and mountains are like a painting—
How many great heroes in one brief moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
When Little Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic bearing radiant and proud.
With a feather fan and silk headscarf,
Amid laughter and talk, he saw enemy ships turn to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders through that ancient land;
Surely my sentimental heart mocks me
For growing grey hairs too soon.
Life in this world is but a dream—
I pour out a cup to offer to the moon on the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves washing away all heroes of the past millennia.
On the western edge of the old stronghold,
People say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling tides dash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
This land and river are painted like a masterpiece;
How many great men arose in that moment alone!

I recall Gongjin’s prime years:
Just married to Xiao Qiao, he was bold and radiant.
With a feather fan and silk scarf,
Laughing and chatting, he saw enemy ships turn to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders through the ancient state;
Perhaps my excessive sentiment makes them laugh at me,
For I have grown grey-haired far too early.
Human life is but a dream;
Let me pour one last libation to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。

Waves wash away all the romantic heroes of a thousand years.
On the west side of the old fortress, people say this is
Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, startling waves beat against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The land and river are like a painting;
How many heroes lived in this one time?
Far back I recall Gongjin in his prime:
Little Qiao had just been married to him, majestic and heroic in bearing.
With feather fan and silk headwrap, chatting and laughing,
Masts and oars turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit travels through the ancient kingdom;
If my sentimental heart were seen, it would surely laugh at me
For having gray hair so early.
Human life is but a dream;
I pour out this cup as an offering to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves washing away all the heroes of a thousand years.
On the western side of these old fortifications,
People say stands Chibi, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms made his mark.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Surging waves crash upon the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
This land is like a painting—
How many great men lived in this brief moment!

I think back to Gongjin in his prime,
When Little Qiao had just become his bride;
His majestic bearing was full of vigor and grace.
With a feather fan and a silk headband,
While laughing and talking, he reduced the enemy’s ships to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders through that ancient kingdom;
If sentimental feelings were laughed at, they’d mock me—
For my hair has turned prematurely white.
Life in this world is but a dream;
I offer a cup of wine to the moon on the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves have washed away
All the heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the ancient fortress, men say
This is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Terrifying waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The land and river are like a painting,
In this moment, how many great heroes!

I recall in my mind Gongjin’s youth,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic bearing was magnificent.
With feather fan and silk headscarf,
He laughed and talked, while the enemy fleet
Turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders back to that old land;
Perhaps romantic souls would laugh at me,
For my hair has turned prematurely white.
Human life is but a dream;
I raise a cup to pour before the river moon."}

To the west of the old ramparts,

Startling waves crash against the shores,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The land and river are like a painting;
How many heroes in that brief moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
Little Qiao having just married him,
His heroic spirit shining with brilliance.
With feather fan and silk headscarf,
Laughing and chatting, warships vanished in ash and smoke.

Sentimental souls must laugh; I’m gray-haired too soon.
Life is but a dream beneath heaven,
So I offer a cup to the moon above the river."}

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。

羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves have washed away
A thousand years of heroes.
West of the ancient ramparts,
Men say, is Zhou Yu’s Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms.
Rocks pierce the sky,
Surging tides crash the shore,
Piling up ten thousand heaps of snow.
The landscape is like a painting—
How many heroes it once held!

I think of Gongjin in his youth,
Just wed to Xiao Qiao,
His heroic bearing so bold and brilliant.
With feather fan and silk cap,
In talk and laughter,
The enemy ships were burned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders to that ancient realm—
If I am too sentimental, let me be laughed at
For my early grey hair.
Life is but a dream—
Let me pour out a cup
To the river and the moon."}

The Great River flows east,
Waves sweeping away thousand-year heroes.
West of the old fortress,
They say this is Red Cliff where Zhou Yu fought.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against shore,
Rolling up heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting;
How many heroes in one moment!

I think back to when Gongjin was young,
Xiao Qiao newly married, his pose heroic and brilliant.
Feather fan and silk headscarf,
While laughing and chatting,
Enemy masts turned to ash and smoke.
Visiting the ancient land in my mind,
My sentimental heart should laugh at me for early grey hair.
This mortal world is but a dream;
Let me pour a libation to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves washing away the heroes of a thousand years.
To the west of the old ramparts,
People say this is Chibi, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms triumphed.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shores,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The land and river are like a painting,
How many heroes arose in that brief moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
When Little Qiao had just been married to him,
His martial figure blazed with brilliance.
With a feather fan and silk handkerchief cap,
Laughing and chatting casually,
He turned enemy ships to ash and smoke.
My soul roams through the ancient state;
If my heart could laugh at me for being overly sentimental,
It would mock my hair, prematurely white.
Life is but a dream beneath heaven,
So I offer this cup of wine to the moon above the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves washing away the heroes of a thousand ages.
On the west side of the ancient fort,
People say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms triumphed.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The landscape is like a painting,
Gathering so many great men in one era.

Distant thoughts turn to Gongjin in his youth,
With Xiao Qiao newly wed,
His heroic spirit shining and bold.
In feather fan and silk scarf,
Laughing and chatting, he reduced enemy ships to ash and smoke.
Spirit roaming over the old kingdom,
Sentimental hearts would laugh at me,
For my hair turned white too soon.
Life is but a dream;
I pour a libation of wine to the river moon."}

To the west of the ancient ramparts,

Surging waves crash against the shores,
Coiling up a thousand piles of snow.
Land and river like a painting,
How many heroes within this moment!

Far back to Gongjin’s prime,
When Little Qiao had just wed him,
His heroic posture radiant and bright.
Feather fan and silk headscarf,
In talking and laughing,
Masts and oars turn to ash, smoke vanishes.
My soul wanders through the old kingdom;
Sentimental thoughts might laugh at me,
For grey hair came too soon.
Human life is but a dream—
I pour one cup, offering to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The great river flows east, its waves sweeping clean all heroes and romance of a thousand ages.
On the western side of the old fortifications, people say this is where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms fought at Red Cliff.
Ragged rocks pierce the sky; startling waves beat against the shore, stirring up a thousand piles of snow.
The mountains and rivers are like a painting—how many heroes emerged in that single era!
Distantly I recall Gongjin in his prime; Little Qiao had just married him, displaying heroic grace.
With a feather fan and silk headscarf, laughing and chatting as enemy ships turned to ash and vanished into smoke.
My spirit wanders through that ancient land; sentimental nature mocks me for my prematurely whitened hair.
Life is but a dream; let me pour a cup of wine to offer to the moon on the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves sweeping away all heroes and romantics of the past millennia.
On the western edge of the old fortifications,
People say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Thundering waves dash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The mountains and rivers are painted like a masterpiece;
How many great men arose in that moment alone!

I recall Gongjin’s prime years:
Just married to Xiao Qiao, his heroic bearing was radiant.
With a feather fan and silk headscarf,
Laughing and chatting, he watched the enemy fleet turn to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders through the ancient state;
Perhaps they would laugh at my excessive sentimentality,
For I have grown grey-haired far too early.
Human life is but a dream;
Let me pour one last libation to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows east,
Its waves sweeping away
All the heroes of ages past.
West of the old ramparts,
They say this is Red Cliff,
Where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms reigned.

Ragged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling tides crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and river are like a painting,
How many great men in one brief moment!

I recall Gongjin in those days,
When Little Qiao had just been wed,
His heroic spirit radiant and bold.
With a feather fan and silk headscarf,
Amidst laughter and conversation,
The enemy fleet turned to ash and smoke.

In my mind I roam the ancient kingdom;
Perhaps they would laugh at my sentimental heart,
Which grew white hair too soon.
Human life is but a dream;
Let me pour a cup of wine
To offer to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The gallant heroes of a thousand ages gone.
West of the ancient fortress, men say,
Stands the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms era.
Jagged rocks pierce the skies, fierce waves crash the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is a painting; how many heroes, in their time!

I think far back of Gongjin in his prime,
Xiao Qiao newly wed, his heroic bearing bright.
With feather fan and silken cap, in his laugh and talk,
The enemy's masts and oars turned to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders to that ancient land;
The sentimental one should laugh at me—
For my hair has turned white too soon.
The world is but a dream; I pour this cup
To the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves sweeping away
The heroes of a thousand years.
On the western side of the old fortifications,
People say this is Red Cliff,
Where Zhou Yu fought in the Three Kingdoms era.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up heaps of snow.
The land and water are like a painting—
How many heroes gathered here at once!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
When Little Qiao had just become his bride;
His posture was heroic and brilliant.
With a feather fan and silk headscarf,
Amid laughter and conversation,
The enemy’s warships turned to ash and smoke.

My soul wanders through the ancient land;
Perhaps my sentimental nature makes me smile,
For I have grown premature gray hair.
Human life is but a dream—
I pour a cup of wine in offering
To the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves sweeping away
The heroes of a thousand years.
On the western side of the old fortifications,
People say this is Red Cliff,
Where Zhou Yu fought in the Three Kingdoms era.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up heaps of snow.
The land and water are like a painting—
How many heroes gathered here at once!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
When Little Qiao had just become his bride;
His posture was heroic and brilliant.
With a feather fan and silk headscarf,
Amid laughter and conversation,
The enemy’s warships turned to ash and smoke.

My soul wanders through the ancient land;
Perhaps my sentimental nature makes me smile,
For I have grown premature gray hair.
Human life is but a dream—
I pour a cup of wine in offering
To the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves washing away the heroes of a thousand years.
To the west of the old ramparts,
They say this is Red Cliff, of General Zhou from the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shores,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The land and river are like a painting;
How many heroes in that brief moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
Little Qiao having just married him,
His heroic spirit shining with brilliance.
With feather fan and silk headscarf,
Laughing and chatting, warships vanished in ash and smoke.
My soul roams the ancient land;
Sentimental souls must laugh at me,
For my hair has turned prematurely white.
Life is but a dream beneath heaven,
So I offer a cup to the moon above the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Waves sweeping away the romantic heroes of a thousand ages.
On the western side of the old fortress,
People say this was Red Cliff, where Zhou Lang fought in the Three Kingdoms.
Ragged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up heaps of snow.
Landscape as picturesque as a painting—
How many heroes gathered here in this single moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride;
His heroic bearing, elegant and bold.
Feather fan and silk headscarf,
While laughing and chatting,
He turned enemy ships to ash and smoke.
Visiting the ancient land in spirit,
My sentimental heart should laugh at me for having grey hair so early.
Human life is but a dream;
Let me offer a cup of wine to the river moon."}

rising like piles of snow.
The land is painted like a picture;

Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
his heroic spirit vivid and bold.
With feather fan and silk headband,

My soul wanders through the ancient kingdom;
if my passionate heart were laughed at by anyone,
it would be because my hair turned white too soon.
Life is but a dream;
I pour this cup as an offering to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Waves wash away heroes of ages past.
To the west of ancient ramparts, men say,
Was Red Cliff where General Zhou held sway.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky's high blue,
Thundering waves crash, foam like snow anew.
The land is a painting so fair and grand,
How many heroes graced this ancient land!

I recall when Gongjin in his prime,
Little Qiao had just become his wife.
With feather fan and silk cap he stood,
Laughing as enemy fleets burned for good.
My soul roams through that kingdom old,
Love makes them mock my premature cold.
White hairs have come too soon to stay;
Life is but a dream, brief as a day.
With a single cup I pour libation,
To the moon reflected in the river's flow."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows east,
Its waves washing away, the heroes of a thousand years.
To the west of the old ramparts,
People say this is Chibi, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms triumphed.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shores,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The land and river are like a painting,
How many heroes arose in that brief moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
When Little Qiao had just been married to him,
His heroic spirit shone with brilliance.
With a feather fan and silk handkerchief cap,
Laughing and chatting casually,
Masts and oars vanished in ash and smoke.
My soul roams through the ancient state;
The sentimental should mock me,
For my hair has prematurely turned white.
Life is but a dream beneath heaven,
So I offer this cup of wine to the moon above the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Waves sweeping away the romantic heroes of a thousand ages.
On the western side of the old fortress,
It is said this was Red Cliff, where Zhou Lang fought in the Three Kingdoms.
Ragged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up heaps of snow.
Landscape as picturesque as a painting—
How many heroes gathered here in one era!

I recall Gongjin in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride;
His heroic bearing, elegant and bold.
Feather fan and silk headscarf,
While laughing and chatting,
He turned masts and oars to ash and smoke.
Visiting the ancient land in spirit,
My sentimental heart should laugh at me for having grey hair so early.
Human life is but a dream;
I pour a libation of wine to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。

羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Waves wash away the heroes of a thousand ages.
To the west of the old fortress, men say
Is Red Cliff of Zhou Lang in the Three Kingdoms.

Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The landscape is like a painting;
How many great heroes gathered in this one time!
I imagine Gongjin of those days,
When Little Qiao had just married him,
His heroic bearing vigorous and spirited.
With feather fan and silk headscarf,
While chatting and laughing, he turned enemy ships to ash and smoke.
My spirit roams through the ancient land;
Sentimental as I am, they would surely laugh at me
For my early graying hair.
Human life is but a dream;
I pour a cup of wine to pay homage to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves washing away the heroes of a thousand years.
West of the ancient fortress, they say
Is Chibi, where young Zhou Lang fought in the Three Kingdoms era.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
Landscape like a painting—
How many great men lived in this one moment!

I recall Gongjin of old days,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic spirit radiant and fierce.
With feather fan and silk sash,
In laughter and casual talk,
He turned enemy masts to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders through the ancient land;
Sentimental as I am, they would laugh at me,
For my hair has already turned white too soon.
Human life is but a dream;
Let me pour this cup of wine to the river moon."}

Churning up heaps of snow.
The land and rivers are like a painting—
How many heroes in their time!

His bearing grand and gallant.
With feather fan and silk cap, at his ease,

Roaming the old kingdom in spirit,
If the tender-hearted should laugh at me,
For my early graying hair—

With a feather fan and silk headscarf, amidst laughter and conversation, enemy ships turned to ash and vanished in smoke.

With a feather fan and silk scarf, while smiling and talking, he turned enemy ships into ash and smoke.

With a feather fan and silk headscarf, while chatting and laughing casually, he caused the enemy's warships to turn into gray ashes and vanish in smoke.
My spirit wanders through this ancient land; perhaps my excessive sentimentality mocks me, causing my hair to turn white too early.
Human life is but a dream; I pour out a cup of wine to pay tribute to the river moon."}

羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting; how many heroes lived in this one hour!
I recall Gongjin in those days—Xiao Qiao had just become his bride—
with martial grace and brilliant spirit.
With feather fan and silk headscarf, while talking and laughing,
enemy ships were ash and smoke, vanished without trace.
My spirit wanders over that ancient land; the sentimental would laugh at me,
who grew grey hair so early.
Human existence is but a dream; I raise a cup to pour libation
to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows eastward,
Its waves sweeping away the romantic heroes of a thousand ages.
To the west of these ancient ramparts, people say,
Is Red Cliff where Zhou Lang triumphed in the Three Kingdoms’ era.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky;
Startling tides crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The rivers and mountains are like a painting—
How many heroes arose in that fleeting moment!

I think back on Gongjin’s prime years,
When Little Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic spirit radiating brilliance.
With feather fan and silk headscarf,
Amidst laughter and talk, enemy masts turned to ash and smoke.

Wandering my spirit through the old kingdom,
Sentimental as I am, they would surely laugh at me,
For I have grown gray-haired too early.
Life is but a dream—
I offer this cup of wine to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows eastward,
Its waves sweeping away the romantic heroes of a thousand ages.
To the west of these ancient ramparts, people say,
Is Red Cliff where Zhou Lang triumphed in the Three Kingdoms’ era.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky;
Startling tides crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The rivers and mountains are like a painting—
How many heroes arose in that fleeting moment!

I think back on Gongjin’s prime years,
When Little Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic spirit radiating brilliance.
With feather fan and silk headscarf,
Amidst laughter and talk, enemy masts turned to ash and smoke.

Wandering my spirit through the old kingdom,
Sentimental as I am, they would surely laugh at me,
For I have grown gray-haired too early.
Life is but a dream—
I offer this cup of wine to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves washing away the heroes of a thousand years.
West of the ancient fortress, it is said, lies Red Cliff,
Where Zhou Yu fought in the Three Kingdoms era.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves beat against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
This land is like a painting;
How many heroes graced this moment!

I recall Gongjin from long ago:
Just after Little Qiao became his bride,
His heroic bearing was splendid and vibrant.
With a feather fan and a silk headscarf,
While chatting and laughing calmly,
He turned the enemy fleet to ash and smoke.

My soul wanders through the ancient kingdom;
If my excessive emotion were visible, they would laugh at me—
For premature white hair has come too early.
Human life is but a dream;
Let me pour a cup of wine to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves wash away all the romantic heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortress,
People say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms made his name.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Surging tides crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand mounds of snow.
The land and river are like a painting;
How many great men arose in that moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime:
Xiao Qiao newly wed, he stood majestic and heroic.
With a feather fan and silk headscarf,
Laughing and chatting, enemy ships turned to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders through ancient times;
The sentimental ancients surely laugh at me,
Who has grown silver early.
Life in this world is but a dream;
Let me simply offer a cup of wine to the moon on the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows east;
Its waves wash away the heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the ancient ramparts, people say,
Is Red Cliff of Zhou Yu from the Three Kingdoms era.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Surging waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and river are like a painting;
How many heroes in this single moment!

Far back I recall Gongjin’s prime,
When Little Qiao had just been wed to him,
His stance heroic, his spirit radiant.
With feather fan and silk kerchief,
Talking and laughing, he turned enemy ships to ash and smoke.
My soul roams the old country;
Sentimental as I am, they might laugh at me
For growing gray hair so early.
Human life is but a dream;
I pour a cup of wine to offer to the moon in the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

This land and river are like a painting—how many great warriors arose in that moment!

I recall how Gongjin (Zhou Yu) was in his youth: Xiao Qiao had just become his bride, and his heroic bearing was magnificent and spirited.
With a feather fan and a silk headscarf, amidst laughter and talk, he made the enemy’s warships turn to ash and vanish in smoke.
My spirit wanders through those ancient days; if they were sentimental, they might laugh at me for my hair turning white so early.
Life in this world is but a dream; I pour out a cup of wine as a libation to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。

Waves wash away heroes of a thousand years.

West of the old ramparts,
It is said that lies Red Cliff
Where Zhou Lang triumphed in the Three Kingdoms.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky;
Startled tides beat the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.

Rivers and mountains are like a painting—
In such times, how many heroes!

Distant thoughts of Gongjin in those days:
Little Qiao had just married him,
His heroic bearing vibrant and fine.

With a feather fan and silk headband,
Amid talk and laughter,
Masts and oars turn to ash and vanish in smoke.

Spirit wanders through the ancient land;
Perhaps my sentimentality mocks me,
For white hair came too early.

Human life is but a dream:
I offer this cup
To the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Waves wash away the heroes of a thousand ages.
To the west of the old bastion, they say,
Is the Red Cliff where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms reigned.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky;
Startled waves beat the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting—
In that era, how many heroes there were!

Far off I recall Gongjin in his prime:
Little Qiao had just become his bride,
His manly bearing radiant and bold.
With a feather fan and silk head-scarf,
He laughed and talked
While enemy ships turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders over that ancient realm;
Sentimental love would surely mock me
For my hair grown prematurely white.
All human life is but a dream—
I pour one cup of wine to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The land and river are magnificent as a painting; how many heroic figures arose in that brief time!

With a feather fan and silk headband, amidst laughter and chat, their warships turned to ash and vanished in smoke.
My spirit wanders through that ancient kingdom; if I am too sentimental, they must laugh at me for my hair turning white so early.
Human existence is but a dream; here I raise a cup of wine and pour it out to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand ages of hills and waters,
No hero can be found where Sun Zhongmou once ruled.
The stages for dance and song,
The romantic elegance, were all swept away by rain and wind.
In the slanting sun among grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say that Ji Nu once lived here.
I recall those days:
Gold-tipped spears and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.
In the Yuanjia era, hasty plans were made,
To seal the altar at Lang Juxu,
Only to earn panicked glances northward.
For forty-three years,
In my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How unbearable to look back:
Beneath the temple of Fuli,
Crowds of crows feed on offerings,
And village drums beat with noise.
Who will ask, as for Lian Po in his old age:
Can he still eat enough rice?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves sweeping away all heroes of a thousand years.
West of the ancient ramparts,
They say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Thunderous waves dash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
Land and river like a painting;
How many great men in that era!

Far back I recall Gongjin’s prime:
Little Qiao newly wed, his heroic air resplendent.
Feather fan and silk scarf,
Amidst laughter and chat, their warships turned to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders in the old land;
The sentimental should laugh at me,
For grey hair came too soon.
Human life is but a dream;
With a cup, I offer wine to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand ages of rivers and hills—
No hero remains to be found
Where Sun Zhongmou once stood.

Dance terraces and singing stages,
All their elegance swept away
By rain and wind.

Slanting sun, grass and trees,
In the commonest lanes and streets—
They say Ji'Nu once lived here.

Think of those years: golden spears, iron-hooved horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia blundered rashly,
Wishing to seal the Wolf Peak;
All he won was to glance northward in panic.

Forty-three years have passed—
In my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires on the Yangzhou road.

How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the Foli Shrine,
A flock of temple crows, the drums of the village feast.

To whom can I ask:
"Lian Po is old—
Can he still eat his fill?""}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand ages of rivers and hills—
No hero remains to be found
Where Sun Zhongmou once stood.

Dance terraces and singing stages,
All their elegance swept away
By rain and wind.

Slanting sun, grass and trees,
In the commonest lanes and streets—
They say Ji'Nu once lived here.

Think of those years: golden spears, iron-hooved horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia blundered rashly,
Wishing to seal the Wolf Peak;
All he won was to glance northward in panic.

Forty-three years have passed—
In my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires on the Yangzhou road.

How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the Foli Shrine,
A flock of temple crows, the drums of the village feast.

To whom can I ask:
"Lian Po is old—
Can he still eat his fill?""}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Jagged rocks pierce the sky; startling waves crash against the shore, rolling up snowflakes by the thousand.
The land and river are like a painting—how many great heroes stood here in that fleeting moment.
I recall Gongjin in his prime: Little Qiao had just become his bride; he stood majestic and spirited.
With a feather fan and silk headband, amidst laughter and banter, the enemy fleet was reduced to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders through ancient realms; perhaps affectionate gods would laugh at me for growing gray so soon.
Life on earth is but a dream; I pour a libation to the moon reflected in the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The gallant figures of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortress, men say, lies
Red Cliff where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms won fame.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, fierce waves slap the shore,
And roll up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting—how many heroes once thronged this scene!

I think back to Gongjin in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride, his bearing grand and bright.
With feather fan and silk cap, amid his talk and laughter,
The enemy masts and oars were scattered to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders to that vanished kingdom—
The passionate in me should laugh at my early grey.
All life is but a dream: I pour this cup
To the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows eastward, washing away, wave by wave, all the heroes of a thousand years.
To the west of these ancient ramparts, they say this is Red Cliff,
Where General Zhou of the Three Kingdoms once stood.
Rugged rocks pierce the sky; roaring waves batter the banks,
Curling up into a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and river are like a painting—
How many great men emerged in that single era!

I recall Gongjin from long ago,
When Little Qiao had just become his bride,
His posture heroic, his spirit radiant.
With a feather fan and a silk turban,
In laughter and ease, he saw enemy ships
Turn to ash and vanish in smoke.
Visiting this ancient realm in my mind,
My sentimental heart must mock me
For having gray hairs before my time.
Human life is but a dream—
So I pour another libation to the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The mountains and rivers are like a painting; how many great warriors arose in that single age?
I think back to Gongjin in his prime: Xiao Qiao had just married him, and he was majestic and spirited.
With a feather fan and a silk headscarf, talking and laughing casually, he scattered the enemy fleet into ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders over the old kingdom; if they saw my excessive sentimentality, they would surely laugh at me for having gray hairs so early.
Human life is but a dream; I raise a cup here to pour it out as libation to the moon on the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows eastward,
Its waves sweeping away all the heroes of a thousand ages.
To the west of the old fortifications,
They say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms triumphed.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The mountains and rivers are like a painting;
How many great men arose in that one era?

I recall Gongjin in those days,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic bearing was vigorous and inspiring.
With a feather fan and silk sash,
Amidst laughter and talk,
The enemy’s warships turned to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders through the ancient land;
Perhaps my sentimental nature should mock me,
Having grown grey-haired too soon.
Life in this world is but a dream;
I pour a cup of wine for the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows eastward,
Its waves sweeping away all the heroes of a thousand ages.
To the west of the old fortifications,
They say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms triumphed.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The mountains and rivers are like a painting;
How many great men arose in that one era?

I recall Gongjin in those days,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic bearing was vigorous and inspiring.
With a feather fan and silk sash,
Amidst laughter and talk,
The enemy’s warships turned to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders through the ancient land;
Perhaps my sentimental nature should mock me,
Having grown grey-haired too soon.
Life in this world is but a dream;
I pour a cup of wine for the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。

Its waves have swept away
All the heroes of a thousand ages.
On the western side of the old fort,
People say this is Red Cliff,
Where General Zhou of the Three Kingdoms made his stand.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky;
Thundering waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The landscape is like a painting—
How many heroes gathered here in that one moment!

I recall Gongjin in those years:
Little Qiao had just become his bride,
His spirit heroic and radiant.
With a feather fan and silk scarf,
Laughing and chatting, he turned the enemy fleet to ash.
My soul roams the ancient land;
Perhaps my sentimental nature mocks me
For growing white hair too soon.
Human life is but a dream—
I pour a cup of wine to toast the river and moon."}

With feather fan and silk headscarf, laughing and chatting, he saw enemy ships turn to ash and smoke.

Life is but a dream; I pour a libation to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand years of land and river, yet heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
Dance halls and song terraces; their elegance is all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sunlight on grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
People say Liu Yu once lived there.
Recall those days: golden spears and iron horses,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand miles, fierce as tigers.
The Yuanjia campaigns were hasty;
Trying to match the glory of sealing Mount Langju,
They won only panic and a glance northward.
For forty-three years, in my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires along the road through Yangzhou.
Who can bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Wolu, crows feast on sacrifices
And drums beat for village rites.
Who asks now: Lian Po is old—
Can he still eat enough to ride?""}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The great river flows east; its waves wash away
all the heroes of a thousand ages.
On the west side of the old fortress,
they say, is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms made his stand.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky; startling waves beat the shore,
rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and waters are like a painting—
in one era, how many heroes arose!
I gaze far back to Gongjin in his prime:
Little Qiao had just become his bride;
bright-eyed he stood, heroic and free.
With a feather fan and silk headscarf,
laughing and chatting, he set the enemy fleet ablaze,
so that masts and oars vanished in smoke and ash.
If my spirit wanders through those ancient lands,
surely they would smile at my passionate heart,
at these white hairs grown too soon.
Human life is but a dream—
I raise a cup to toast the moon above the river."}

羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

by Su Shi
The Great River flows eastward; waves wash away all the heroes of a thousand ages.
On the west side of the old fortress, people say this is Red Cliff where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky; roaring waves crash against the shore, rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The land and river are like a painting. How many great men gathered in that single moment!
I recall Gongjin in his prime: Little Qiao had just married him, and he was majestic, with heroic spirit shining forth.
With a crane-feather fan and silk headscarf, laughing and chatting, enemy fleets turned to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders through the ancient kingdom; my sentimental nature would surely be laughed at by those who see me prematurely graying.
Human life is but a dream. Let me pour another libation to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Across a thousand autumns, the rivers and mountains remain,
But nowhere can one seek Sun Quan, that hero of old.
The stages for dance and song, the elegance and grandeur
Have all been swept away by rain and wind.
Amidst slanting sun, grasses, and trees,
In ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say this was where Liu Yu once lived.
I recall those days: gold spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

The Yuanjia era rushed into action carelessly,
Trying to seal victory at Langju Xu,
And earned only panic and looking north in fear.
For forty-three years now, within my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires along the roads to Yangzhou.
Who has the heart to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Tuoba Tao,
Crowds caw and drums beat for folk rites.
Who is there to ask:
Is Lian Po too old? Can he still eat rice?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "To the Tune of Niannujiao: Thoughts on Red Cliff
The Great River flows east, its waves washing away heroes from a thousand ages.
On the west side of the old fortress, people say this is Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky; roaring waves crash against the shore, rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The rivers and mountains are like a painting—how many heroes emerged in that single era!
Far back I recall Gongjin in his prime: Little Qiao had just married him, his stance heroic and splendid.
With feather fan and silk headscarf, laughing and chatting, he set their warships ablaze until they turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders over the ancient land; perhaps my sentimental nature mocks me for premature gray hair.
Human life is but a dream—I pour a cup of wine to toast the river moon."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "**Eternal Joy: Memories of the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou**

For a thousand ages, this land and water remain;
We seek for heroes, yet find none like Sun Zhongmou.
The singing stages and dancing terraces are gone,
Their romantic splendor swept away by wind and rain.

Beneath the slanting sun, amidst grass and trees,
In common lanes and streets, they say Liu Yu once lived.
I recall those days—golden spears and iron horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles, fierce as tigers.

In Yuanjia years, haste led to error;
They tried to seal the triumph at Langju Mountain,
But earned only panic, looking north in fear.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in sight
Are the beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.

Who can bear to look back?
At the shrine of Wolu, beneath its eaves,
Crows caw loudly, drums beat for village rites.
Who now asks: though Lian Po is old,
Can he still eat well enough to fight?""}

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

On the west side of the old fortress, people say this is Red Cliff of Zhou Yu from the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky; startling waves beat against the shore, rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The landscape is like a painting; in that time, how many heroes there were!
I recall Gongjin in his prime, when Little Qiao had just married him, with an imposing and spirited bearing.
With a feather fan and silk headscarf, while talking and laughing, the enemy's masts and oars turned to ash and vanished in smoke.
My spirit wanders through the ancient land; perhaps my sentimentality causes others to laugh at me for having premature gray hair.
Life on earth is but a dream; I pour a libation to the river moon."}

Dance halls and singing terraces—romantic elegance has all been swept away by wind and rain.
The setting sun shines on grass and trees; in ordinary lanes and streets, people say that Liu Yu once lived here.
Recalling those years: golden spears and iron horses, their spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
In Yuanjia, recklessly he sought to seal the peak of Langju, only gaining hasty retreat and looking north in panic.
Forty-three years have passed; in my gaze I still remember the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back? Beneath the Temple of Buddha, crows feed on offerings, drums thunder for spirits.
Who will ask me, as Lian Po aged, "Can you still eat enough for war?""}

Where can one seek heroes like Sun Zhongmou?
Dance stages and song platforms,
Their elegance swept away by wind and rain.
The slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
They say Liu Yu once lived here.
Thinking back to those years:
Golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles, fierce as a tiger.

The Yuanjia era rushed hasty plans,
To seal the mound at Langju Mountain,
Only gaining a panicked look northward.
For forty-three years,
Even now in sight I remember
The beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the temple of Fuli (Tuoba Tao),
Crowds of crows gather, drums beat loudly.
Who will ask,
"Though Lian Po is old,

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "To the Tune of Niannujiao: Meditating on the Ancient Past at Red Cliff

The great river flows eastward, its waves sweeping away all the romantic figures of a thousand ages. West of the old ramparts, it is said to be Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms held sway.

Jagged stones pierce the sky; startling waves crash against the shore, rolling up a thousand stacks of snow. The land and water are like a painting—how many heroes graced this moment in time!

I recall Gongjin in his prime, when he had just married Xiao Qiao, with heroic elegance radiantly displayed. With a feather fan and silk headscarf, chatting and laughing, he turned the enemy fleet to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders through that ancient realm; perhaps my sentimental nature would laugh at me for growing silver hair so early. Human life is but a dream—I pour a cup of wine as an offering to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "<Forever Joyful: Memories at the North Fort of Jingkou>

Majestic rivers and mountains stand for a thousand ages,
Yet nowhere can we find Sun Zhongmou, the hero of old.
Dance halls and singing terraces have vanished into dust;
The glamour of those days has been washed away by rain and wind.
Under the slanting sun among wild grasses and trees,
In ordinary lanes and alleys, it is said that young Liu Yu once lived.
I recall how, in those years, his golden halberds and iron horses
Swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger in its rage.

In Yuanjia’s hasty campaigns, seeking to seal rites at Mount Langjuxu,
He gained only panic as he looked back northward in fear.
For forty-three years, my gaze still remembers the beacon fires
That lit up the road to Yangzhou. Who could bear to look back?
At the shrine of Foxian, crows feast on offerings while drums beat loudly for society gods.
Who asks if Lian Po, though aged, can yet eat well enough to ride?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Across a thousand ages, the land and river endure,
But we find no hero like Sun Quan.
Dance pavilions and song terraces—their romance
Has all been swept away by wind and rain.
By the slanting sun and grassy trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
Think of those days: golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit roaring to swallow ten thousand li like a tiger.
In Yuanjia's haste, seeking to seal victory at Langjuxu,
He gained only panicked glances backward toward the north.
Forty-three years—looking out, I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back? Beneath the shrine of Wolf-Boy,
A crowd of sacrificial crows and village drums.
Who will ask, as did Zhao Hui for General Lian Po:
"Though old, does he yet have the strength to eat?""}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River surges east,
Its waves sweeping away all heroes of a thousand years.
West of the ancient ramparts,
They say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Thunderous waves dash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
Land and river like a painting;
How many great men in that age!

Far back I recall Gongjin’s prime:
Little Qiao newly wed, his heroic air resplendent.
Feather fan and silk scarf,
Amidst laughter and chat, their warships turned to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders in the old land;
The sentimental should laugh at me,
For grey hair came too soon.
Human life is but a dream;
With a cup, I pour wine to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River surges east,
Its waves sweeping away all heroes of a thousand years.
West of the ancient ramparts,
They say this is Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Thunderous waves dash against the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
Land and river like a painting;
How many great men in that age!

Far back I recall Gongjin’s prime:
Little Qiao newly wed, his heroic air resplendent.
Feather fan and silk scarf,
Amidst laughter and chat, their warships turned to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders in the old land;
The sentimental should laugh at me,
For grey hair came too soon.
Human life is but a dream;
With a cup, I pour wine to the moon over the river."}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand years of rivers and mountains;
No hero can be found
In the place of Sun Quan.
The dance halls and singing terraces,
Their elegance all swept away
By rain and wind.
In the slanting sun, among grass and trees,
On ordinary streets,
People say that Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those days:
golden spears and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuan Jia acted hastily,
Sought to seal the altar at Langjuxu,
And gained only panicked looks toward the north.
Forty-three years on,
As I gaze out, I still remember
Beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
Can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of the Toba ruler,
Flocks of sacred crows peck at offerings,
Drums sound in the village festival.
Who will ask me—
Is Lian Po too old now?
Still able to eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

Heroes like Sun Zhongmou are nowhere to be found.
Dancing stages and singing towers,
Their romantic splendor was all washed away
By wind and rain.
Slanting sun, grass and trees,
Ordinary lanes and streets—
People say this is where Liu Yu once lived.
Recall those days: gold spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
In Yuanjia, hasty preparations were made
To seal the victory at Langjuxu,
But only won panic-stricken glances northward.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still recall
The beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fuli
Crows feed on offerings, drums beat for sacrifices.
Who asks now if Lian Po, though old,
Can still eat well enough to serve?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy
Composed at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou, Reflecting on the Past

For a thousand ages this land and stream endure,
Yet where is Sun Zhongmou, the hero of old?
Stages for dance and terraces for song once flourished,
But their elegance has all been swept away by wind and rain.
The setting sun slants over grass and trees,
In common lanes and alleys, locals say it was here that Ji Nu lived.
Think of those years: golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia acted hastily, aiming to seal the peak of Langju,
Only to earn a hurried glance northward in panic.
Forty-three years have passed; looking out, I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Who can bear to look back? At the temple of Foli,
A flock of ravens caws amidst the drums of folk sacrifice.
Who is there to ask: Is Lian Po grown old?
Can he still eat rice and ride into war?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy
Composed at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou, Reflecting on the Past

For a thousand ages this land and stream endure,
Yet where is Sun Zhongmou, the hero of old?
Stages for dance and terraces for song once flourished,
But their elegance has all been swept away by wind and rain.
The setting sun slants over grass and trees,
In common lanes and alleys, locals say it was here that Ji Nu lived.
Think of those years: golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia acted hastily, aiming to seal the peak of Langju,
Only to earn a hurried glance northward in panic.
Forty-three years have passed; looking out, I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Who can bear to look back? At the temple of Foli,
A flock of ravens caws amidst the drums of folk sacrifice.
Who is there to ask: Is Lian Po grown old?
Can he still eat rice and ride into war?"}

For a thousand ages, this river and these mountains stand,
Yet nowhere to find the heroes of old—
Like Sun Quan, Lord Zhongmou.
The dance stages and singing terraces fade;
Their romantic elegance swept away
By rain and wind.
Amid setting suns, grass, and trees,
In humble lanes and common streets,
People say that Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those years: golden lances and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

But Yuanjia’s hasty plans failed,
Aiming to seal Mount Langju,
Only to flee northward in panic.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Tuoba Tao,
Crows caw and folk drums beat.
Who asks now, like General Lian Po,
Old as he is, can he still eat well?"}

Millennia of mountains and rivers remain; nowhere to find a hero like Sun Zhongmou.
Dance stages and song terraces—their romance all swept away by wind and rain.
In slanting sun among grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and streets, people say Liliu once lived there.
Recall those days: golden spears and iron horses, spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia era’s hasty campaign—to seal Wolf Mountain—ended only with panicked glances northward.
Forty-three years; still remember in my gaze the beacon fires along Yangzhou road.
How can I bear looking back? At the shrine of Foxi, crows gather amid festival drums.
Who asks me now: Is General Lian Po too old—can he still eat rice well?"}

For a thousand ages the mountains and rivers have stood, but heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
Dancing terraces and singing platforms—their glamour was swept away by wind and rain.
In the slanting sun among grass and trees, in common lanes and alleys, people say that Liu Yu once lived there.
I recall those years: iron horses with gold-tipped spears, their spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

The Yuanjia era rushed hastily; they sought to seal Mount Langju, but only gained panicked glances back to the north.
Over forty-three years ago, within my sight I still remember the beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Who can bear to look back? Beneath the shrine of Tuoba Tao, crows feed on offerings and drums sound for sacrifices.
Who asks if Lian Po, though old, can still eat enough to ride into battle?"}

Composing at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou, Thinking of Antiquity

For a thousand ages the rivers and mountains endure,
But where can one seek the hero Sun Zhongmou?
The stages for dance and song are silent now;
All elegant grace has been swept away by rain and wind.
Beneath the slanting sun among grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and alleys, people say Lord Ji once lived here.
I recall those days: golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

The Yuanjia era rushed carelessly to seal Mount Langjuxu,
Only earning hasty retreats and fearful glances north.
Forty-three years have passed; looking across,
I still remember the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
Is it bearable to look back? Beneath the Buddha-Wolf Temple,
Crows gather over offerings, drums beat for society rites.
Who will ask, as Lian Po grew old:
Are you still fit enough to eat a meal?""}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy
Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

Mountains and rivers endure through thousand ages;
No hero like Sun Quan remains to be found.
Dance stages and song pavilions lie silent,
Their glory swept away by wind and rain.
Amid slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those days:
Golden halberds and iron steeds,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand li fierce as a tiger.

Yuanjia’s northern campaign was rash,
Aiming to seal Langju Mountain,
Only to earn a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember
Beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
At the Shrine of Fuli (the Northern Invader),
Crows cry over offerings, drums beat in village rites—
A deafening indifference.
Who will come to ask?
General Lian Po is old—is he still fit to wield his sword?"}

By Xin Qiji

For thousand years this land and river remain,
Yet heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
Stages for dancing and singing have crumbled;
The elegance of bygone days has all been swept away by wind and rain.
Amidst slanting sun, grasses, and trees, in ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say that Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those days when his golden halberds and iron steeds
Swallowed up ten thousand miles with tiger-like vigor.

In Yuanjia times, hasty preparations were made
To seal victory atop Mount Langju,
Only earning a panicked glance northward.
Over forty-three years since then,
As I gaze into the distance, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Is it bearable to look back?
Beneath the shrine of the Northern barbarian lord,
Crows of the gods peck at offerings while village drums beat.
Who will ask me, now an old man like Lian Po:
"Are you still able to eat meals?""}

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

On the west side of the old fortifications, people say it was Red Cliff where General Zhou of the Three Kingdoms once stood.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky; startling waves crash against the shore, rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and river are like a painting—how many great heroes gathered here in one era?
I recall Gongjin in his prime: Xiao Qiao had just married him; he was majestic and spirited.
With a feather fan and silk cap, he laughed and talked as enemy ships turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders through the ancient land; my sentimental nature should be laughed at by me, for I have grayed too early.
Human life is but a dream—let me pour this cup onto the moon over the river."}

For a thousand years, this land and these waters remain,
But nowhere can we seek out heroes like Sun Quan.
The dance stages and song terraces are gone;

Beneath the slanting sun, amidst grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say that Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those days—golden spears and iron horses,
A spirit devouring ten thousand miles, fierce as tigers.

In Yuanjia’s haste they sought to seal Langju Mountain,
Yet won only panic, looking north in fear.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in my sight,
The beacon fires along the road through Yangzhou burned bright.

Can one bear to look back?
At the shrine of Fuli,
Crows caw and drums beat for communal rites.
Who asks if Lian Po, though old,
Can still eat well enough to serve?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Nostalgia at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

A thousand ages pass, yet rivers and mountains remain;
No place to find heroes like Sun Zhongmou.
Dance stages and singing terraces have vanished,
Their romantic grace swept away by rain and wind.
Amid slanting suns, grass, and trees,
In common lanes and humble streets,
People say Liu Yu once dwelt here.
I recall those days of the Great Marshal Liu: golden lances and iron horses,
His ambition swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

But Emperor Wen’s Yuanjia campaigns were rashly hurried,
Seeking to seal Mount Langju, only gaining a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
At the shrine of the foreign emperor Tuoba,
Sacred crows feed while rustic drums beat in indifferent clamor.
Who asks now, if old General Lian Po,
Though aged, is fit for war?"}

For a thousand ages, mountains and rivers remain;
Nowhere to find the heroes of old,
Not even Sun Zhongmou.
The dance pavilions, song stages—
Their romantic grandeur is swept away
By rain’s beat and wind’s blow.

In slanting sun among grass and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say Jinu once lived here.
Think of those years past:
Gold halberds, iron horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign,
To seal Langju’s peak in triumph—
Only earned a panicked glance northward.

Forty-three years;
Looking out, I still recall
The beacon fires along Yangzhou’s road.

How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fuli,
A flock of sacred crows and village drums.

Who asks now if Lian Po, growing old,
Can still eat?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy
Reflections at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

For a thousand ages, mountains and rivers remain;
No hero like Sun Zhongmou can be found.
Stages for dance and platforms for song,
Their romantic splendor has been swept away by wind and rain.
Setting sun on grass and trees,
Ordinary lanes and alleys—
People say this is where Liu Yu once lived.
Recalling those years:
Golden spears and iron horses,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

In Yuanjia times, hasty ambitions aimed to seal the victory at Langju Mountain,
Only earning a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years have passed;
Gazing out, I still remember the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How could one bear to look back?
At Fo Li Temple,
crows feed on offerings amidst village drums.
Who will come to ask,
Like Lian Po: Is he too old to eat well enough to fight?"}

For a thousand years, this river and mountain stand,
Yet heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
The dance stages and singing terraces have vanished;
Their glory was swept away by wind and rain.
In the slanting sun, among grass and trees,
People say that Liu Yu once lived in these humble lanes.
I recall those days of golden spears and iron horses,
When his spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

The Yuanjia campaign was hasty and ill-prepared;
Seeking to seal victory at Wolf Mountain,
He earned only frantic retreats looking north in fear.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to turn back?
Beneath the shrine of Fuli,
Crows caw around the folk drums.
Who asks now, as of old General Lian Po:
Though aged, can he still eat enough for war?"}

Through ages, this land and these waters remain.
Where can we find heroes like Sun Quan?
Dance stages and song terraces are gone;
Their elegance swept away by rain and wind’s relentless throng.

Beneath slanting sun, amidst grass and trees,
In humble streets where ordinary lives unfold,
People say Liu Yu once made his home there.
I recall those days—golden spears and iron steeds,
A spirit that devoured ten thousand miles, fierce as a tiger.

In Yuanjia years, haste led to failure;
Attempting to seal triumph at Langju Mountain,
They gained only panic, looking north in fear.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in sight,
The beacon fires along the road through Yangzhou burned bright.

Can one bear to look back?
At the shrine of Wolu beneath its eaves,
Crows caw loudly, drums beat for folk rites.
Who asks now: though Lian Po is old,
Can he still eat well enough to serve?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy · Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou
By Xin Qiji

For a thousand ages, this land and river stand;
No hero like Sun Zhongmou can be found.
The dancing halls and singing terraces,
Their elegance washed away by wind and rain.
In slanting sun among grass and trees,
Common lanes and streets,
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
Recall those days: golden spears and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

The Yuanjia era rushed with folly,
Trying to seal Mount Langju,
Only gained frantic northward glances.
Forty-three years have passed;
Still in my sight I remember
Beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How could one bear to look back?
Under the Fobi Temple,
Crowds of crows and drums of worship.
Who will ask, like Lian Po grown old—
"Can you still eat and serve?""}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

For a thousand ages, mountains and rivers endure,
But where is Sun Quan, the hero of old?
The stages for dance and song lie empty now;
All romantic glory has been swept away by rain and wind.
In the slanting sun, among grass and trees,
In common lanes and alleys, people say this was once Liu Yu’s home.
I recall those years: golden halberds and iron steeds,
A spirit devouring ten thousand miles, fierce as tiger.

In Yuanjia, hasty plans were made—
To seal victory at Langjuxu, they gained only panic, turning north to look back in fear.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in my gaze
Are the beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Is it bearable to look back? Beneath Buddha-Li’s temple,
Crow cries and drum beats mark village sacrifices.
Who will ask, like General Lian Po grown old:
"Can you still eat?""}

A thousand years of mountains and rivers;
Nowhere to seek the hero Sun Quan.
The dancing stages and singing terraces are gone;
All elegance swept away
By wind and rain.
In the slanting sun among weeds and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say young Liu Yu once lived here.
Recall those days—gold spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Hasty expeditions in Yuanjia,
To seal triumph on Langxü Mountain,
Won only frantic glances toward the north.
Forty-three years passed; through my gaze I still remember
Beacon fires along Yangzhou’s roads.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fuli,
Crows feast on offerings, village drums beat loud.
Who asks now: Old Lian Po is aged,
Yet can he still eat enough?"}

For a thousand ages, the mountains and rivers remain,
But where is Sun Zhongmou, that hero of old?
The stages for dance and song have crumbled;
All romance and vigor washed away by wind and rain.
Sunset gilds the grass and trees;
In common lanes and alleys, they say
Liu Yu once lived.
Think back to those years:
Golden halberds, iron horses—
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

In Yuanjia's haste,
He sought to seal victory at Mount Langju,
But won only frantic glances northward.
Forty-three years on,
As I gaze, I still recall
The beacon fires along Yangzhou's roads.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Toba Tao,
Crows feast on offerings, drums beat for earth spirits.
Who asks me now?
Like Lian Po growing old—
Can he still eat rice and wield a sword?"}

For a thousand ages, the rivers and mountains remain,
Yet nowhere can we find Sun Zhongmou of heroic fame.
The stages for dance and song, the elegant charm they held,
Have all been washed away, as wind and rain expelled.
Amidst slanting sun, grass, and trees, in common lanes,
They say Liu Yu once lived here, amidst humble plains.
I recall those years when weapons gleamed like gold,
Horses clad in iron thundered, bold and cold;
Their spirit swallowed ten thousand miles, fierce as tigers.

In Yuanjia era, hasty ambitions were raised high,
To seal success beyond Langju Mountain’s sky,
But only fled back north with panic-stricken eyes.
Forty-three years have passed; looking out, I still see
The beacon fires along Yangzhou’s path burning free.
How can I bear to look back? Near Buddha Li’s shrine,
Crows flock to sacrifices, drums beat fine.
Who is there to ask me, now that Lian Po is old:
Can he yet eat enough to wield his sword?"}

A thousand years of mountains and rivers;
Nowhere to seek the hero Sun Quan.
The dancing stages and singing terraces are gone;
All elegance and romance swept away
By wind and rain.
In the slanting sun among weeds and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say young Liu Yu once lived here.
Recall those days—gold spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Hasty expeditions in Yuanjia,
To seal triumph on Langxü Mountain,
Won only frantic glances toward the north.
Forty-three years passed; through my gaze I still remember
Beacon fires along Yangzhou’s roads.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fuli,
Sacred crows feast while village drums beat loud.
Who asks now: Old Lian Po is aged,
Yet can he still eat enough?"}

A thousand autumns of rivers and mountains;
Nowhere to find Sun Quan’s heroic spirit.
Dance halls and singing terraces,
The grace and power were all washed away by rain and wind.
In the setting sun’s light on grass and trees,
In common alleys and streets,
They say Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those days:
Golden spears and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

The Yuanjia era rushed carelessly,
To seal the mound at Langju,
Gaining only a panicked glance back north.
Forty-three years later,
Still vivid in my gaze:
Beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.

Who can bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of the barbarian king,
One hears crows’ cries and village drums.
Who asks me now,
Like General Lian Po grown old,
Can this body still eat well?"}
