凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Reflecting on the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

Through countless ages, mountains and rivers remain,
But where can one now seek the hero Sun Zhongmou?
The dance floors and singing terraces are gone;
Their glamour was swept away by wind and rain.

Amidst slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say that here once lived Xu De,
Who, in his youth, with golden spears and iron horses,
Swallowed ten thousand miles of territory like a tiger.

Yet rashly, under Emperor Yuanjia's reign,
They sought to seal victory at Mount Langju,
And gained only panic, looking north in fear.

Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still recall the beacon fires
That lit up the road to Yangzhou.

How unbearable it is to look back!
Beneath the shrine of the barbarian king,
Crows caw and drums beat for common rites.

Who will ask me, as they asked Lian Po:
"Though old, can he still eat enough
To ride into battle?""}

For a thousand ages, the rivers and mountains remain,
But nowhere can we find heroes like Sun Zhongmou.
The stages of dance and song, the elegance of their times,
Have all been swept away by wind and rain.
In the slanting sun among grass and trees,
Within common lanes and alleys,
They say Liu Yu once lived here.
Thinking back to those years:
Golden spears and iron horses,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

In Yuanjia, haste led to rash action,
Attempting to seal victory at Langjuxu,
Only earning panicked glances northward.
Forty-three years later,
Looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How painful to look back!
Beneath the shrine of Fuli,
Crows eat offerings, drums beat for village rites.
Who will ask me,
Like the old Lian Po,
If I can still eat enough rice?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

For a thousand ages, this land and river remain,
But where is Sun Zhongmou, the hero we seek in vain?
Dance stages and song terraces have long since gone;
The romance they held was swept by wind and rain.
In slanting sunlight, trees and grass appear,
In common lanes, people say Liu Yu once lived here.
Think back to those days: iron horses, golden spears,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like tigers fierce.
In Yuanjia’s haste, they tried to seal Langjuxu’s peak,
Only winning frantic glances northward as they fled.
Forty-three years have passed; I still remember clearly
The beacon fires along Yangzhou’s roads of red.
Can one bear to look back? Under Fuli’s temple shrine,
Crowds caw and drums beat for spirits, blind and deaf. 
Who asks the question, with old General Lian Po now:
'Are you still fit to eat, and take the sword again?'"}

Dancing pavilions and singing terraces—their glamour was swept away by wind and rain.
Amid the setting sun and wild grass, along common lanes and streets,
People say that Emperor Liu Yu once lived here.
Think back to those years: golden spears and iron steeds,

Beneath the shrine of Northern Wei's emperor,
Crowds gather for sacrifices, crows feed on offerings.
Who now asks if Lian Po, though old,
Can still eat enough to ride into battle?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "Thinking of You, Nianu Jiao: Recalling the Past at Red Cliff

The Great River flows east, its waves washing away countless heroes of the past.
On the western side of the ancient fortress, men say this is the Red Cliff where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky; startling waves crash against the shore, rolling up a thousand piles of snow.
The land and river are like a painting—how many great heroes rose in that single era!

I imagine Gongjin in his prime: Xiao Qiao had just become his bride, his bearing heroic and spirited.
With a feather fan and a silk headband, he laughed and chatted as enemy ships turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders through that ancient kingdom; my sentimental heart surely mocks me for my early white hair.
Human life is but a dream—I pour out my wine to honor the moon upon the river."}

For a thousand ages this land and river remain,
Yet no hero can be found where Sun Quan once reigned.
Dance stages and singing platforms, with all their charm and grace,
Have been swept away by wind and rain through time and space.
Beneath the slanting sun, among grass and trees of common lanes,
People say here lived Liu Yu, who rose from humble plains.
I recall those years when golden spears and iron horses charged,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like tigers enraged.

The Yuanjia era rushed to claim glory on Wolf Mountain’s peak,
Only to earn hasty retreat, looking north in panic bleak.
Forty-three years have passed; I still remember clearly now
The beacon fires that lit the road to Yangzhou’s boughs.
Is it bearable to look back? Beneath the shrine of Tuoba Tao,
Crows feast on offerings while drums beat for local show.
Who asks if Lian Po, old as he is, can still eat enough
To ride again to battle, proving his strength tough?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

For millennia, this land and river have endured,
Yet heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
Dance halls and singing terraces—
Their glamour swept away by rain and wind.
Amidst slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say little Liu Yu once lived here.
Think of those years: Golden halberds and iron horses,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand li, fierce as tigers.

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign aimed at sealing Mount Langju,
But won only a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years on, looking afar, I still recall
The beacon flames along the road to Yangzhou.
How unbearable to look back!
At the shrine of Fuli, crows scavenge the offerings,
And village drums sound for pagan rites.
Who now asks of Lian Po, grown old:
Can he still eat enough to ride into battle?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "Thoughts on the Past at Red Cliff

The Great River flows east, its waves washing away all heroes of ages past.
On the western side of the old fort, they say, lies the Red Cliff where Zhou Yu won glory in the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky; roaring waves batter the shore, rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and river are like a painting—how many great men gathered here in one fleeting moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime: Little Qiao had just married him then, and he stood majestic, full of heroic spirit.
With a feather fan and silk scarf, he laughed and talked as enemy ships turned to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders through that ancient kingdom; if my emotions were too deep, they would mock me—for gray hair already covers my temples.
Life is but a dream; I pour this cup of wine to honor the moon over the river."}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

Over a thousand years, the mountains and rivers remain,
Yet heroes like Sun Zhongmou are nowhere to be found.
The stages of dance and song have faded,
Their elegance swept away by wind and rain.
Amid the slanting sun and grassy trees,
In ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those days:
Golden spears, iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

In the Yuanjia era, hasty ambitions sought
To seal the mound of Langjuxu,
But only won a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the temple of Foli,
Crows feast on offerings, drums of sacrifice resound.
Who will ask me, now that I am old like Lian Po,
Still able to eat enough rice for war?""}

For millennia, mountains and rivers endure;
No heroes remain to be sought in Sun Quan’s haunts.
The terraced stages for dance and song—
Their elegance and vigor have all been swept away by rain and wind.
In slanting sunlight among grass and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say it was here that Liu Yu once lived.
Thinking back to those days:
Golden halberds and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

The Yuanjia era was hasty,
Attempting to seal victory atop Mount Langju,
Only to earn a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years pass;
Gazing into the distance, I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of the Wei emperor,
Crowds of crows flock, drums beat for folk rites.
Who now asks: Is Lian Po grown old?
Can he still eat well enough to ride?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

Millennia pass, yet mountains and rivers endure;
Where are the heroes now? No trace of Sun Quan’s might.
Stages for dance and song lie silent in decay;
All romance swept away by wind and rain’s relentless sway.

Beneath the slanting sun, through grass and common lanes,
They say this was the home of Liu Yu long ago.
I recall those days—golden halberds, iron steeds,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger’s roar.

But Yuanjia’s haste sought glory, to seal the mound at Langju,
Only earning panic-stricken glances northward fled.
Forty-three years have passed; my gaze still holds remembrance
Of beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou burning red.

Can I bear to look back? Beneath the temple of Tuoba Tao,
Crows feast on offerings, drums beat in village rites’ dull glow.
Who asks if Lian Po, old though he is, can still eat well?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

For ages uncounted, mountains and rivers have endured,
Yet heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
The stages for dance and song, where elegance once reigned,
Have been swept away by wind and driving rain.

In slanting sun and grassy trees, within common lanes,
People say the young emperor Liu Yu once lived here.
Recall those early days: his gold-tipped spears, iron steeds,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand li, fierce as tigers.

Hasty was the Yuanjia campaign’s grand design,
To seal the altar at Langju Mountain’s summit high,
It only won him panic, glancing back northward in fear.
Forty-three years have passed; looking out, I still recall
The beacon fires lighting up the road to Yangzhou.

Can one bear to look back? Beneath Buddha Fox Temple,
Crows circle wildly, drums beat for folk sacrifices.
Who now asks, like of General Lian Po: “Though old,
Can you still eat a meal?”"}

For a thousand ages, mountains and rivers remain;
No hero like Sun Quan can be found again.
Dance halls and singing stages have gone to dust,
The charm of those days washed away by wind and rain.
In slanting sun and weeds, on ordinary lanes,
Men say this was where Liu Yu once resided.
I think back to when he led armored horses, golden spears,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger roaring.

Yuanjia rushed his campaign, seeking glory at Langju Mountain,
And won only frantic retreat, glancing north in panic.
Forty-three years pass; looking out, I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.

Who now asks if Lian Po, old as he is,
Can still eat enough rice—and ride into battle?"}

For millennia, this land and river have endured,
Yet heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
Dance halls and singing terraces—
Their glamour swept away by rain and wind.
Amidst slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
Think of those years: Golden halberds and iron horses,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand li, fierce as tigers.

Yuanjia’s reckless campaign aimed at sealing Wolong Mountain,
But won only a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years on, looking afar, I still recall
The beacon flames along the road to Yangzhou.
How unbearable to look back!
At the shrine of Fuli, crows gather round,
And village drums beat for local rites.
Who now asks of Lian Po, grown old:
Can he still eat?"}

Dancing stages and singing terraces—romantic elegance has all been swept away by wind and rain.
Sunset slants over grass and trees, common lanes and alleys, where people say Liu Yu once lived.
Recall those years when golden spears and iron horses charged forward, their spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia’s hasty campaign to seal Mount Wolf aimed for glory, only to win frantic retreat and glance northward in fear.

Who asks if Lian Po, though old, can still eat enough to ride into battle?"}

By rain and wind.
In slanting sunlight among grass and trees,

Gold-tipped spears and iron-armored horses,

Beneath the shrine of Fuli,
A chorus of crows and drumbeats fills the air.
Who comes to ask me,
Like General Lianpo in his old age:
Can you still eat enough to ride into battle?"}

Through ages, this land and river remain,
But heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
The pavilions of dance and stages of song,
Their romantic grace washed away by wind and rain.
By slanting sun and grassy trees, in common lanes,
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
Recalling those days, with golden halberds and iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

In Yuanjia's haste, he sought to seal the victory at Wolong Mountain,
Only winning a panicked look northward in retreat.
For forty-three years I have watched,
Still remembering the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the temple of Woyang,
Crows feast and drums beat for spirits.
Who asks if Lian Po, now old,
Can still eat enough to go to war?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

For thousand years this land and river stand,
Yet heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere found.
The stages built for dance and song remain,
But all their elegance has been swept clean—
By pounding rain and driving wind erased.

Beneath the slanting sun, among wild grass,
In humble lanes where common folk reside,
They say that Liu Yu once called this place home.
I think of those days: golden halberds gleamed,
Iron-shod horses thundered through the plains;
Their spirit swallowed ten thousand miles, fierce as tigers.

In Yuanjia’s reign, haste led to folly’s end,
With hopes to seal victory on Mount Langxu,
They gained only panic, looking north in fear.
Forty-three years have passed since then, but still,
When I gaze across, I recall vividly
The beacon fires lighting up the roads from Yangzhou.

Is it worth turning back to look again?
At the shrine of Tuoba Tao, crows descend
To peck at offerings, while village drums resound.
Who now would ask, as one might ask of Lian Po:
Though old, can he still eat well enough to fight?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

For a thousand ages the rivers and mountains stand,
Yet no hero like Sun Quan can be found.
The gleaming stages and singing halls remain,
But their splendor was swept away by wind and rain.
In slanting sunlight, amidst grass and trees,
Ordinary lanes hold memories that freeze:
Here Liu Yu once lived, humble in his day,
Who later drove foes back with iron might and cavalry display.
He dreamed of glory as generals of old,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles bold.

Emperor Wenjia acted rashly in haste,
Sought to seal Mount Langju, but met disgrace;
Only fled homeward, looking north in fear.
Forty-three years have passed since I was here;
I still recall the beacon fires ablaze
Along the roads to Yangzhou, through smoke and haze.
How painful to look back upon this scene:
Beneath Buddha's shrine, crows feed on offerings keen,
With drums beating for spirits in the land.
Who asks if Lian Po, though aged, yet strong hand
Can wield sword and shield? Can he eat enough?
To serve the state, does he retain his stuff?"}

For a thousand ages, this land and river remain,
But no hero like Sun Zhongmou can be found again.
The stages where dance and song once charmed the air,
All elegance swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grassy trees, in ordinary lanes,
People say where Liu Yu once lived in humble homes.
Thinking back to those days: gold spears, iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger’s roar.

In Yuanjia he rushed blindly, seeking glory’s seal,
To climb Wolf Mountain’s peak, only to flee in haste,
Looking northward in panic, his ambition failed.
Forty-three years have passed; in my gaze I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou burning bright.
How dare one look back? At Lord Fox’s shrine below,
Crowds of crows eat offerings, drums beat for folk rites.
Who will ask, as with old Lian Po:
Is he fit enough to eat, and ready to fight?"}

Ten thousand years of mountains and rivers—
Where now to find a hero like Sun Zhongmou?
The dance terraces and singing stages,
Elegance and romance, all washed away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In the common lanes and alleys,
Men say the place where Jinu once lived.
Recall those days: golden spears, iron-hooved steeds,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia’s hasty campaign—
Wishing to seal the Wolf Mountain—
Won only a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years, still I remember gazing out,
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
A flock of crows and drums of festival rites.
Who will ask whether old Lian Po,
Though aged, can still eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

Through ages, this land and river remain,
But heroes like Sun Quan are found no more.
Where once stood stages for song and dance,
The glamour of those days has been swept away
By wind and rain’s relentless force.

Amid slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say young Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those years when gold-tipped spears and iron horses
Charged forward, their spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

In Yuanjia’s haste, they sought to seal rites on Mount Langju,
Only to win frantic glances back toward the north.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember the beacon fires
That lit the road to Yangzhou.

How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
Crows flock with drums of folk worship.
Who now will ask,
“Old General Lian Po—is he still fit for battle?”"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

Through ages, this land and river remain,
But heroes like Sun Quan are found no more.
Where once stood stages for song and dance,
The glamour of those days has been swept away
By wind and rain’s relentless force.

Amid slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say young Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those years when gold-tipped spears and iron horses
Charged forward, their spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

In Yuanjia’s haste, they sought to seal rites on Mount Langju,
Only to win frantic glances back toward the north.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember the beacon fires
That lit the road to Yangzhou.

How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
Crows flock with drums of folk worship.
Who now will ask,
“Old General Lian Po—is he still fit for battle?”"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at North Garrison Pavilion, Jingkou
Through a thousand ages, mountains and rivers remain;
No heroes like Sun Zhongmou can be found.
The stages of dance and song, the romantic grace,
Have all been washed away by rain and wind.
Slanting sun over grass and trees, ordinary lanes and alleys—
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
Thinking back to those days,
golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
In Yuanjia years, hasty campaigns were launched,
To seal glory at Langjuxu,
Only winning a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years since then,
In my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
Who can bear to look back?
At the shrine of Tolien,
One sees only crows eating offerings and drums playing for rites.
Who asks me now:
Is General Lian Po too old? Can he still eat?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

Thousand years of this land and river,
Nowhere to seek a hero like Sun Zhongmou.
Dance pavilions and singing terraces,
Their grandeur all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun, grass and trees,
Common streets and lanes,
People say that Liu Yu once lived here.
Think of those days:
Golden spears and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

In Yuanjia, hasty plans were made,
To seal the altar at Langjusxu,
Only winning a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years;
In my sight I still remember
The beacon fires along Yangzhou's road.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the temple of Fuli,
A chorus of crows and drums for sacrifices.
Who asks now:
Is Lian Po too old?
Can he still eat well?"}

in common lanes, they say Liu Yu once lived.
I recall those years:

breathing in ten thousand miles like tigers.

winnng only frantic glances northward.

the beacon fires along Yangzhou’s road.

At the shrine of Foli,

Who asks: Is General Lian Po old?
Can he still eat enough to fight?"}

Hasty Yuanjia campaigns sought the glory of sealing Mount Langju, yet only earned a frantic glance northward in defeat. 四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

Millennia of rivers and mountains remain,
Where heroes are sought in vain—Sun Quan’s place is empty now.
Dance stages and singing terraces,
The romance of old has been swept away by wind and rain.
In slanting sun, among grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say that Liu Yu once lived there.
I recall those years:
Golden spears and iron horses,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

The Yuanjia era rushed to glory,
To seal triumphs on Langju Mountain,
Only winning frantic glances northward.
Forty-three years pass;
Even now, looking afar, I remember
Beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
Who can bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Tuoba Tao,
Crows feast and drums sound for offerings.
But who asks of Lian Po,
Old as he is—
Can he still eat well, ready to fight?""}

Dancing terraces and singing platforms—all that grace has been swept away by rain and wind.
In the slanting sun among grass and trees, an ordinary lane and street—people say Liu Yu once lived here.
Think of those years: golden halberds and iron horses, his spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

The Yuanjia era rushed into war, aiming to seal the victory at Mount Langju, only gaining frantic glances northward in retreat.
Forty-three years—I remember clearly in my gaze the beacon fires along the roads to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back? Beneath the shrine of Fuli, a chorus of sacred crows and communal drums.

舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

For millennia, this land and river have endured,
Yet heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
Dance halls and singing terraces—
Their glamour swept away by rain and wind.
Amidst slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say little Liu Yu once lived here.
Think of those years: Golden halberds and iron horses,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand li, fierce as tigers.

The Yuanjia emperor, rash, sought glory like Ho Qubing's seal on Langju Xu,
But gained only a fearful backward look.
Forty-three years on, looking afar, I still recall
The beacon flames along the road to Yangzhou.
How unbearable to look back!
At the shrine of Fuli, crows scavenge the offerings,
And village drums sound for pagan rites.
Who now asks of Lian Po, grown old:
Can he still eat enough to ride into battle?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal rivers and mountains,
No hero to find—where is Sun Zhongmou?
Stages of dance and song are gone,
All romance swept away by rain and wind.
Slanting sun, grass and trees,
Ordinary lanes and alleys,
They say Jinu once lived here.
Think of those years: golden halberds, iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed in haste,
To seal Wolf Mountain’s peak,
Only gained a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years later,
Looking out, I still remember
Beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath Foli’s temple,
A swarm of sacred crows, community drums beating.
Who asks now: Old Lian Po,
Can he still eat rice?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal are the mountains and rivers;
No hero like Sun Zhongmou can be found.
Dance stages and song terraces—
All traces of their romantic grace have been swept away by rain and wind.
In the slanting sun, among grass and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say Liu Yu once dwelt here.
I recall those years:
Golden spears and iron horses, their spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

In Yuanjia's era, they rushed to emulate sealing Wolf Hill,
Yet gained only a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath Fo Li’s shrine, crows feed on offerings amidst village drums.
But who asks now: "Like old Lianpo,
Can he still eat?""}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For a thousand ages, this land and river remain,
Yet no trace of the hero Sun Zhongmou is found.
The stages for dance and song have vanished;
Their elegance was swept away by wind and rain.
Amidst slanting sun, grass, and trees, in common lanes and streets,
It is said that Liu Yu once resided here.
One recalls those years: golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.
In Yuanjia, hasty preparations were made to seal the altar at Langjuxu,
Only gaining a panicked glance northward in defeat.
Forty-three years on; looking out, I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Who can bear to look back? Beneath the shrine of Fo Li,
Crowds feast with crows and drums sound their beat.
Who now asks: though General Lian Po is old,
Can he still eat well enough for war?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For a thousand ages, mountains and rivers remain;
No hero like Sun Zhongmou can be found.
The stages and terraces of song are gone;
All their grace has been swept away by wind and rain.
In the slanting sun among grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those years when spears gleamed and horses charged,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like tigers.
Yuanjia acted rashly in seeking glory at Langjuxu,
And only gained a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of the Tuoba king,
Crows feed on offerings, drums sound for harvest rites.
Who asks: Is Lian Po still old?
Can he yet eat a meal?""}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For a Thousand Years: Meditating on the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

To this thousand-year-old land and river, there is no place to find a hero like Sun Quan.
Dancing halls and singing terraces have vanished; their romantic elegance swept away by rain and wind.
In the slanting sun among grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and alleys, people say Liu Yu once lived here.
Thinking of those years, with golden spears and iron horses, his spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

In the Yuanjia era, hastily seeking to seal the mound of Langju (imitating Huo Qubing's victory), they only won chaotic retreats and fearful glances northward.
Forty-three years later, looking out, I still remember the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can I bear to look back? At the shrine of Tuoba Tao, crows feed on offerings, and drums beat for folk rites.
Who comes to ask: Is General Lian Po too old? Can he still eat well?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For a thousand ages this land and river remain;
No hero to seek, like Sun Zhongmou of old.
Dance pavilions and song stages,
The romantic glories have all been washed away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun over grass and trees,
Common lanes and alleys,
People say that Ji Nu once lived here.
Recall those days: golden spears and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
In Yuanjia they hasted rashly,
To seal the mound at Langju,
And won only hurried retreat, looking north in panic.
Forty-three years;
In my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fo Li,
Crowds caw and drums beat for social rites.
Who will ask, like Lian Po grown old:
"Is he yet able to eat rice?""}

But where to seek the hero Sun Zhongmou?
The pavilions of dance and stages of song—
All that romance was swept away by wind and rain.
Beneath the setting sun among grass and trees,
in common lanes and alleys, they say
Liu Yu once lived. I think back to those years:
golden halberds and iron horses,
his spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.
In Yuanjia times, rushed into action,
he sought to seal the mount of Langjuxu,
yet only won a hurried glance northward in defeat.
Over forty-three years; still in my sight,
I remember the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
Who could bear to look back? Beneath Fuli’s shrine,
crows gather for offerings, ritual drums resound.
Who asks now: Is Lian Po old?
Can he still eat his fill?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternally Joyful: Remembering the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

For a thousand years, these mountains and rivers remain,
Yet nowhere can heroes be found among Sun Zhongmou's haunts.
The stages of dance and song are gone;
All elegance and romance have been swept away
By wind and rain.
In the slanting sun, amid grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say that Jino once lived here.
Recalling those days, with golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

The Yuanjia campaign was hasty and ill-prepared;
They sought to seal their triumph atop Mount Langxü,
But earned only frantic glances toward the north.
Forty-three years pass; looking back, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Is it bearable to look back?
Beneath the temple of Fuli,
A flock of sacred crows and the beat of village drums.
Who comes to ask now:
'Lian Po is old—can he still eat well?'"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

Thousand-year rivers and mountains remain;
No hero like Sun Zhongmou is to be found.
Stages for dance and song have vanished;
All romance washed away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun, grass, trees,
Common lanes and alleys—
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
Recall those years: iron horses, golden spears,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

In Yuanjia era, hasty plans to seal Lang Juxu,
Only gained panicked looks northward.
Forty-three years pass;
Still remember in sight
Beacon fires along Yangzhou road.

How bear to look back?
Under Fuli Temple,
A crowding of ritual drums and crows.
Who asks? Lian Po, old now—
Can he still eat well?"}

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Immortal rivers and mountains, where no hero can be found—no Sun Zhongmou.
Dance stages and song terraces: their elegance all swept away by rain and wind.
Slanting sun, grass and trees, common lanes and streets—people say Liu Yu once lived here.
Recall those years: golden spears, iron horses; spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia’s hasty campaign to seal the Wolf Mound only earned panicked northward glances.
Forty-three years: even in sight, I still remember beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
Who could bear to look back? Beneath the Buddha’s shrine, a flock of sacred crows, drums and rites.
Who would ask if Lian Po, now aged, still has the strength to eat well?"}

With golden spears, swallowed ten thousand miles
Like a tiger in one breath.

Only winning panic as they looked northward in despair.

The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For a thousand ages, the mountains and rivers remain,
But nowhere can one find heroes like Sun Quan.
The singing stages and dancing platforms have vanished;
All romantic splendor was swept away by wind and rain.
Amidst the slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say that Liu Yu once lived here.
One recalls those years when golden halberds and iron horses
Swallowed ten thousand miles with the ferocity of a tiger.
Yuanjia acted hastily, hoping to seal the mound at Langjuxu,
But won only panicked glances northward in retreat.
Forty-three years later, looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fo Li,
A clamor of sacred crows and village drums.
Who will ask, as they did of Lian Po:
"Though old, can he still eat?""}

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For a thousand ages, the rivers and mountains remain,
Yet heroes like Sun Zhongmou are nowhere to be found.
The stages for dance and song have vanished;
Their romantic glory was swept away by rain and wind.
In the setting sun, among grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say that Jinu once lived there.
Thinking of those years past:
Golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

In Yuanjia, plans were hasty,
He sought to seal victory at Mount Langju,
But only won panic-stricken glances northward.
Forty-three years have passed,
Looking across, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
Crows caw loudly as folk drums beat.
Who asks if Lian Po, though old,
Can still eat enough rice?"}

Yet no hero like Sun Zhongmou can be found.
The singing stages and dancing terraces are gone;
Their romantic grace has been swept away
By rain and wind.
In the slanting sun, among grassy trees
And ordinary lanes,
They say that Ji Nu once lived here.
One recalls those years:
Steel halberds and iron horses,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand li, fierce as tigers.

In Yuanjia, he acted rashly,
Seeking to seal the victory at Langju Xu,
But only earned a hasty retreat, looking north in panic.
For forty-three years,
As I gaze afar, I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How could one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fo Li,
Crows feast on offerings and drums beat for rituals.
Who is there to ask:
Is Lian Po old now?
Can he still eat well?"}

No hero can be found where Sun Zhongmou once was.
The dancing halls and singing terraces,
Their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
Recalling those days: golden halberds, iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Under Yuanjia's careless rule, seeking to seal Wolfs Hill,
He only won hasty retreats, glancing back northward in fear.
Forty-three years have passed; looking out, I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How could one bear to look back?
Beneath the temple of Fubai,
A flock of crows gathers, drums sound for sacrifices.
Who asks now if Lian Po, grown old,
Is still fit to eat his meals?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For thousands of years, the rivers and mountains remain,
but where can one find a hero like Sun Quan?
The stages for dance and song,
the elegant grandeur—all washed away
by wind and rain.
In the slanting sunset, among grass and trees,
in ordinary lanes and alleys,
people say that Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those days:
golden spears and iron horses,
a spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

The Yuanjia reign rushed hastily,
attempting to seal the summit of Mount Langju,
yet winning only panicked glances northward in retreat.
Forty-three years have passed;
even now, looking out, I remember
the beacons burning along the road to Yangzhou.
How unbearable to look back—
under the temple of Foxi,
crows feast on offerings to the gods,
and village drums beat solemnly.
Who will come to ask me,
as if inquiring of old General Lian Po:
'Are you still fit enough to eat?'"}

But no heroes like Sun Zhongmou are to be found.
The stages for dance and song have faded,
Their splendor swept away by wind and rain.

In common streets and lanes, they say Liu Yu once lived.
I recall those years: golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit devouring thousands of miles like a tiger.

In Yuanjia’s haste, seeking glory from sealing the Wolf Mountain,
He earned only panic, looking north in fear.
Forty-three years have passed; even now, gazing afar,
I remember the beacon fires burning along Yangzhou’s roads.

Who will ask me, as one asked Lian Po when he grew old:
“Can you still eat enough rice?”"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Immortal land and waters, yet heroes are nowhere to be found,
No trace of Sun Zhongmou.
The stages where dance and song once echoed,
All their glamour washed away by rain and wind.
Over grass and trees slants the setting sun;
In common lanes and alleys, people say
Liu Yu, known as 'Ji Nu', once lived here.
Thinking back to those years: spears of gold, horses in iron armor,
Their spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia acted hastily, seeking glory at Mount Langju,
Only winning panic-stricken glances northward.
For forty-three years, gazing afar, I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back? Beneath the temple of Fuli,
Crows feast on offerings, drums beat for village rites.
Who will come to ask, like King of Zhao asking Lian Po:
'Are you old now? Can you still eat enough to fight?'"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For a thousand years, the land and rivers remain,
But heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
The stages of dance and song,
All elegance has been swept away by wind and rain.
In slanting sunlight on grass and trees,
Along ordinary lanes, people say Liu Yu once lived here.
Think back to those days: iron horses, golden spears,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia's hasty campaign sought glory at Langxuju,
Only to gain frantic looks north in retreat.
Forty-three years later, in my gaze I still recall
The beacon fires along Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back? Beneath Fuli's shrine,
Crows feed on offerings, drumbeats ring for the harvest god.
Who comes to ask: Is General Lian Po old yet?
Can he still eat well enough to ride?"}

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

I recall those days: iron horses and golden spears, with a spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia’s haste to seal the Wolf Mountain only earned a panicked glance northward. Forty-three years on, gazing ahead, I still remember beacon fires along the Yangzhou road. Can one bear to look back? Beneath the shrine of Toba Tao, crows feast and drums boom for community rites. Who comes to ask: Is General Lian Po old yet, can he still eat rice?"}

Dance stages and singing towers; their romance has all been swept away by rain and wind.
In the slanting sun among grass and trees, in common lanes and alleys, people say Liu Yu once lived.
Think of those years: golden spears and iron horses, with spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia acted rashly, seeking to seal the Xiuju Mountain, but won only hurried northward glances.
Forty-three years on; looking out, I still remember the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
Who can bear to look back? Beneath the shrine of Woli, crows feast and drums beat for the sacrifices.
Who will ask about me, old as Lian Po—am I still fit to eat?"}

The setting sun over grass and trees, common lanes and streets—

To think of those years: golden spears and iron horses,

For a thousand years, this land and river endure,
Yet no heroes like Sun Zhongmou remain.
The dance stages and singing terraces have vanished;
All their glamour swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun, grass, trees, common lanes,
People say Jinu once lived here.
Think of those days: gold spears, iron steeds,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia’s court rashly sought Mount Langju’s seal,
But earned only panicked glances northward.
Forty-three years on, I still recall
The beacon fires along Yangzhou’s road.
Who can bear to look back?
At Fuli’s shrine, sacred crows scavenge,
And village drums beat in oblivious merriment.
Who asks now of old Lian Po:
Can he still eat enough for war?"}

Where can we find heroes like Sun Quan?
Dance stages and song terraces are gone;
Their elegance blown away by wind and rain.

Beneath slanting sun, amidst grass and trees,
In humble streets where ordinary lives unfold,
People say Liu Yu once made his home there.
I recall those days—golden spears and iron steeds,
A spirit that could swallow ten thousand miles, fierce as a tiger.

In Yuanjia years, haste led to failure;
Attempting to seal triumph at Langju Mountain,
He was left with only panic, glancing north in fear.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in sight,
The beacon fires along the road through Yangzhou burned bright.

Can one bear to look back?
At Bili's shrine below,
Crows caw loudly, drums beat for folk rites.
Who asks now: though Lian Po is old,
Is his appetite still good?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For thousands of years, this land and river endure,
But where can one find heroes like Sun Quan?
The pavilions for dance and stages for song,
All their elegance swept away by wind and rain.

In the slanting sun, among grass and trees,
Within common lanes and ordinary streets,
They say Liu Yu once lived here long ago.
I recall those days: gold spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Hasty were the plans of Yuanjia’s reign,
To seal the mound at Langjuxu in glory—
Only to earn a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years have passed; looking out,
I still remember the beacon fires along Yangzhou’s road.

How dare I look back to the shrine of Foli,
Where crows feast on sacrificial flesh,
And drums beat loud at folk festivals.
Who cares to ask: Is Lian Po too old now?
Can he yet eat well enough for battle?"}

For a thousand ages, mountains and rivers remain,
But heroes like Sun Zhongmou cannot be found.
Stages for dance and song have vanished;
Their glamour has been swept away by wind and rain.
In the slanting sun among trees and shrubs,
In ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say that Emperor Wu once lived there.
I recall those days: golden halberds and iron horses,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

The Yuanjia era was rushed,
Aiming to seal victory on Wolf Peak,
But only gained a hurried glance northward.
Forty-three years later,
As I gaze into the distance, I still remember
The beacon fires along Yangzhou’s road.
How painful to look back!
Under the shrine of Foli,
Crows gather for offerings, drums sound socially.
Who will come and ask me,
Like Lian Po in his old age:
Are you still able to eat?"}

斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

But nowhere can one find a hero like Sun Quan.
The stages of dance, the platforms of song,
Romantic fame has all been swept away by wind and rain.
Where slanting sun lights grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say that Liu Yu once lived here.
I think of those days: gold spears and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
In Yuanjia, things were done hastily;
They sought to seal Mount Langju,
Only winning hurried glances northward.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along Yangzhou's roads.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fotuli,
Crows caw and drums sound in ritual feasts.
Who is there to ask:
Lian Po is old—
Can he still eat enough?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For ages past, the mountains and rivers remain,
Yet searching for a hero like Sun Zhongmou, one finds only empty space.
Dance pavilions and singing terraces—
Their romantic splendor washed away by wind and rain.
Under slanting sun, among trees and grass,
In ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say that Jinu once lived here.
Think back to those years: golden halberds and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand li, fierce as a tiger.

The Yuanjia campaigns were rash and hurried,
Aiming to seal Langju Xu, but winning only
a panicked glance toward the North.
Forty-three years have passed; looking afar, I still remember
the beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How painful to look back!
Beneath the Shrine of Fuli,
crows pick at the divine offerings,
and village drums beat for folk festivals.
Who is there to ask me, an old man like Lian Po:
"Can you still eat enough?""}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For ages past this land and river have remained,
But heroes like Sun Zhongmou are nowhere found.
Dance stages, song terraces, their amorous flair
All swept away by rain and driving wind.
In slanting light among the grass and trees,
In common lanes and streets, they say that once
The lad Liu Yu lived here. I think of how
He drove his iron chariots with gold spears,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
In Yuanjia he rashly sought to seal Mount Langju,
Only gaining a panicked retreat, looking north in fear.
Forty-three years on; as I gaze out, I still recall
The beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can I bear to look back? At the temple of the barbarian king,
Crows devour offerings, drums beat for sacrifices.
Who asks if General Lian Po, now old,
Still eats enough to ride into battle?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Millennia have passed over these mountains and rivers;
Where is Sun Quan, the hero of old? He cannot be found.
The pavilions for dance and stages for song are gone;
Their romantic grace has all been swept away
By rain and wind.
Amid the slanting sun and wild grass,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say that Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those years when golden spears and iron horses rushed forth,
With a spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

In the Yuanjia era, hasty preparations were made,
To seal victory at Mount Langju,
But only panicked glances northward were gained.
For forty-three years, looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Who can bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fox Li,
Crows eat offerings while community drums beat.
Who will ask: Is General Lian Po too old?
Can he still eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For a thousand ages, the mountains and rivers endure,
Yet no heroes like Sun Quan can be found.
Dancing pavilions and singing stages fade;
Their romantic glory is swept away
By rain and wind alike.
In the slanted sun, among grass and trees,
On common streets and lanes,
People say that young Liu Yu once dwelled here.
I recall those years of old:
Golden spears and iron horses charged,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like tigers.

The Yuanjia era rushed into action in haste,
Attempting to seal victory atop Mount Langju,
Only to win a panicked glance back north.
Forty-three years have passed since then;
Looking toward the horizon, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How unbearable it is to look back!
Beneath the shrine of Fuli,
A flock of crows pecks at offerings,
While drums beat for local spirits.
Who will come to ask me, like General Lian Po grown old:
"Can you still eat enough rice to ride to war?""}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Perpetual Joy: Meditating on the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

Through a thousand ages, rivers and mountains endure,
Yet nowhere can one find Sun Quan, the hero of old.
Dance stages and song terraces have crumbled away;
Their grace and charm were swept off by wind and rain's cold hold.
In the slanting sun, among grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and streets,
People say Liu Yu, 'Ji Nu', once dwelt in this place.
I recall those years when golden spears and iron horses galloped,
And their spirit swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger's embrace.

In Yuanjia's day, haste led to reckless ambition,
To seal triumphs atop Mount Langju they sought,
Only winning back with panic-stricken glances northward.
Forty-three years have passed; looking out, I still remember clearly
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou burning wildly.
Can I bear to look back? Beneath the shrine of Fuli,
Crows feast on offerings while drums beat for village rites.
Who now would question General Lian Po in his age?
"Though old," he asks, "can I still eat and ride?""}

Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

For a thousand ages, this land and river remain,
But where is Sun Zhongmou, the hero we seek in vain?
The stages of dance and song have long since crumbled to dust,
All romance washed away by wind and rain.
Amidst slanting sun, grass, and trees,
In common streets and alleys, they say Liu Yu once lived here.
Think back to those years:
With golden spears and iron horses,
His spirit swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

In the Yuanjia era, haste led to ruin;
He sought to seal his victory at Langjuxu,
Only to gain a panicked glance northward in defeat.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Tuoba Tao,
Crows feast on offerings while drums thunder in praise.
Who now would ask, 'Like Lian Po grown old,
Can he still eat enough to wield a sword?'"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For thousand ages, rivers and mountains remain,
Yet heroes like Sun Zhongmou are nowhere to find.
Dance stages and song terraces fade;
Their fleeting glory swept away by wind and rain.
Amid slanting suns, grass, and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
People say Jinu once resided here.
I recall those days: golden halberds and iron horses,
His spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

But Yuanjia was rash; aiming to seal victory on the Wolf Mountain,
He won only a panicked glance toward the north.
Forty-three years have passed;
Gazing out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
Is it bearable to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Buddha Li,
Crows caw and folk drums beat.
Who asks now? Like Lian Po grown old,
Can he still eat his fill?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Thousand ages of mountains and rivers;
No hero like Sun Zhongmou remains to be found.
Dance stages and song pavilions,
Their romantic grandeur swept away by rain and wind.
Where the setting sun glows on grass and trees,
In common lanes and alleys,
People say Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those years:
Golden spears and iron horses, their spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia was hasty in ambition, aiming for Langju Mountain,
Only to earn a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years have passed;
Looking out, I still remember the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
At Fo Li Temple, crows feed on offerings to drums of the spring festival.
Who will ask me, like old Lianpo:
"Can you still eat enough to fight?""}

In humble streets where ordinary lives unfold,

For a thousand ages, rivers and mountains remain,
But heroes like Sun Quan are nowhere to be found.
The dance stages and song terraces,
Their elegance swept away by rain and wind.
In the slanting sun among trees and grasses,
Ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say that Liu Yu once lived here.
Think of those years: golden spears and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

Hasty preparations in the Yuanjia era,
To seal victory at Mount Langju,
Only earned frantic glances northward in retreat.
Forty-three years later,
Looking out, I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Under the temple of Fo Li,
Crows feed on offerings, drums sound for rites.
Who will ask me, "Like Lian Po grown old,
Can he still eat enough?""}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For millennia the land and rivers stand,
Where heroes like Sun Quan can't be found.
Stages for song and dance now lie in ruins;
The romance of old has been washed away by rain and wind.
In slanting sun, among trees and common lanes,
People say where Liu Yu once resided.
Thinking back to those days:
Golden spears and iron horses,
Spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia rushed carelessly to seal Wolf Mountain,
Winning only frantic glances northward.
Forty-three years passed;
In my gaze I still remember
Beacon fires along Yangzhou's road.
Who can bear looking back?
Under Buddha's shrine,
Crows gather at temple drums.
Who asks: Is Lian Po too old,
Can he still eat well and fight?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Perpetual Joy: Meditating on the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

For a thousand ages, this land and river have endured,
Yet no place remains to seek Sun Zhongmou, that hero of old.
The pavilions for dance and stages for song,
All traces of elegance were swept away by wind and rain.
In the slanting sun, among grass and trees,
In common lanes and streets, they say Liu Yu once lived.
Recall those years when spears gleamed like gold, horses clad in iron,
Their spirit swallowing ten thousand li, fierce as tigers.

The Yuanjia era was rushed and ill-prepared,
An attempt to seal victory at Langjuxu,
Which won only frantic glances back toward the north.
Forty-three years later, looking out across the land,
I still remember the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the temple of Fuli,
Crows eat sacrificial offerings, drums sound for folk rites.
Who now asks if Lian Po, though aged,

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For a thousand ages, this land and river remain; nowhere to find heroes like Sun Zhongmo.
Dance stages and song terraces are gone; their elegance swept away by wind and rain.
In the setting sun, among grass and trees of common lanes, people say Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those years: iron horses and golden halberds, his spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
In Yuanjia's haste, seeking to seal victory at Langju Mountain, he only won frantic looks northward in retreat.
Forty-three years on, looking out, I still remember beacon fires along Yangzhou roads.

I scratch my white hair until it grows thinner,
So sparse it can no longer hold a hairpin."}

无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。

The wind is fierce, the sky high, gibbons cry in grief; on islets clear and sand white, birds wheel and return.
Endless falling leaves rustle down; the never-ending Yangtze River rolls on.
For ten thousand li, sorrowing over autumn, I have long been a wanderer; for a hundred years, plagued by illness, I alone climb the terrace.
Hardship and bitter regret have frosted my temples thick; broken down, I have newly ceased to raise my cup of turbid wine."}

Clear islet, white sand—birds wheel overhead in flight.

Far from home, I grieve autumn’s desolate chill,
A lifelong traveler, weary and ill.
Old age presses: sickness mounts, I climb alone,
To face the view beneath a fading sun.

Hardship and sorrow frost my temples’ hair;
Ruined by fate, now even wine is denied me there."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。

The wind is sharp, the sky vast; gibbons wail in grief.
The islet clear, sand white; birds circle and return.
Boundless falling leaves rustle down unceasing,
The endless Yangtze rolls on without end.
Far from home, I mourn autumn, a guest for ten thousand miles;
In this lifetime, plagued by illness, I climb the tower alone.
Hardships and bitter regrets have frosted my temples;
Impoverished now, I have just stopped raising my cup of turbid wine."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。"}, "translation": "On Ascending the Heights

The wind is fierce, the sky high; gibbons cry mournfully.
The islet clear, sand white; birds circle back.
Endless falling leaves rustle down without end,
The ceaseless Yangtze rolls in without bounds.
Ten thousand miles of autumn sorrow make me a perpetual wanderer,
In this lifetime riddled with illness, I climb the terrace alone.
Hardships and bitter regrets frost my temples gray;
Impoverished, I have just ceased to drink from my turbid wine cup."}

无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。

The wind is fierce, the sky high, and gibbon cries sound mournful; the islet clear, sand white, birds circle back.
Endless falling leaves rustle down; the unending Yangtze River rolls in.

Hardship and bitter regret have whitened my thick frost-like hair; down on luck, I have just stopped drinking from the muddy wine cup."}

A lifetime riddled by illness, I climb this terrace alone.
Hardship and deep regret whiten my temples with frost;

In my life's hundred years, burdened by illness, I climb the terrace alone.

Downcast and worn, I have newly ceased my cup of turbid wine."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。"}, "translation": "The wind is fierce, the sky high; apes wail in grief.
Islets clear, sands white; birds circle back and forth.
Boundless falling leaves rustle down unendingly,
The ceaseless Yangtze rolls on forever.

In this aged life, beset by illness, I climb the terrace alone.
Hardship and bitter regret have frosted my temples grey;
Wretched and destitute, I have newly ceased to drink from my turbid cup."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。

The islet clear, sand white; birds circle back.
Endless falling leaves rustle down;
The never-ending Yangtze rolls on.

In this long life, sick often, I climb the terrace alone.
Hardship and bitter regret have frosted my temples;
Wretched now, I have just stopped raising the turbid wine cup."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。

Islets clear, sand white; birds circle back and forth.
Boundless falling leaves rustle down endlessly;
The Yangtze River rolls on without end.

A hundred years of illness; I climb the terrace alone.
Hardship and bitter regret have thickened frost on my temples;
In ruin, I have newly stopped raising my wine cup."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。"}, "translation": "The wind is sharp, the sky high; apes cry out in grief.
Islets are clear, sands white; birds circle back to roost.
Endlessly, falling leaves rustle down;
Without end, the Yangtze rolls and flows on.
Far from home, I grieve this autumn, forever a traveler.
A lifetime of sickness, yet I climb alone to this height.
Hardship and bitter regret have whitened my temples;
In ruin, I have just stopped raising my cup of turbid wine."}

All my life ill, I climb the terrace alone.
Hardships and bitter regrets have frosted my temples grey.
Wretched now, I have recently had to stop my turbid wine."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。"}, "translation": "The wind is sharp, the sky high, apes wail in grief;
Clean islets, white sands, birds swirl and return.
Endless falling leaves rustle down in desolation,
The Yangtze's endless torrents surge on forever.

A lifetime of illness leaves me alone upon this terrace.
Hardship and bitter regret frost my gray temples,
Down and out, I have just stopped drinking cloudy wine."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。"}, "translation": "The wind is sharp, the sky high; gibbons wail in grief.
Islets are clear, sand white; birds circle back and forth.
Boundless falling leaves rustle down without end.
The ceaseless Yangtze rolls onward, surging with might.
A thousand miles of autumn sorrow; a long-time wanderer.
A lifetime plagued by illness; alone I climb this terrace.
Hardship and bitter regret have frosted my temples grey.
In ruin and decay, I’ve just ceased to drink my turbid wine."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。"}, "translation": "The wind is sharp, the sky high; gibbons wail in grief.
Islets are clear, sand white; birds circle back and forth.
Boundless falling leaves rustle down without end.
The ceaseless Yangtze rolls onward, surging with might.
A thousand miles of autumn sorrow; always a wanderer.
A lifetime plagued by illness; alone I climb this terrace.
Hardship and bitter regret have frosted my temples grey.
In ruin and decay, I’ve just ceased to drink my muddy wine."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。"}, "translation": "Wind is fierce, the sky high; gibbons wail in grief.
Islets are clear, sand white; birds circle and return.
Endless falling leaves rustle down,
The unceasing Yangtze rolls onward.
For ten thousand li, sorrowing at autumn, I have long been a wandering guest;
In this hundred-year life, plagued by illness, I alone ascend the terrace.
Hardships and bitter regrets have thickened my frost-white temples;
My fortunes are ruined, and I have just ceased to hold the turbid wine cup."}

{"source": {"title": "琵琶行", "author": "白居易", "text": "浔阳江头夜送客，枫叶荻花秋瑟瑟。
主人下马客在船，举酒欲饮无管弦。
醉不成欢惨将别，别时茫茫江浸月。
忽闻水上琵琶声，主人忘归客不发。
寻声暗问弹者谁，琵琶声停欲语迟。
移船相近邀相见，添酒回灯重开宴。
千呼万唤始出来，犹抱琵琶半遮面。
转轴拨弦三两声，未成曲调先有情。
弦弦掩抑声声思，似诉平生不得志。
低眉信手续续弹，说尽心中无限事。
轻拢慢捻抹复挑，初为霓裳后六幺。
大弦嘈嘈如急雨，小弦切切如私语。
嘈嘈切切错杂弹，大珠小珠落玉盘。
间关莺语花底滑，幽咽泉流冰下难。
冰泉冷涩弦凝绝，凝绝不通声暂歇。
别有幽愁暗恨生，此时无声胜有声。
银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。
曲终收拨当心画，四弦一声如裂帛。
东船西舫悄无言，唯见江心秋月白。
沉吟放拨插弦中，整顿衣裳起敛容。
自言本是京城女，家在虾蟆陵下住。
十三学得琵琶成，名属教坊第一部。
曲罢曾教善才服，妆成每被秋娘妒。
五陵年少争缠头，一曲红绡不知数。
钿头银篦击节碎，血色罗裙翻酒污。
今年欢笑复明年，秋月春风等闲度。
弟走从军阿姨死，暮去朝来颜色故。
门前冷落鞍马稀，老大嫁作商人妇。
商人重利轻别离，前月浮梁买茶去。
去来江口守空船，绕船月明江水寒。
夜深忽梦少年事，梦啼妆泪红阑干。
我闻琵琶已叹息，又闻此语重唧唧。
同是天涯沦落人，相逢何必曾相识！
我从去年辞帝京，谪居卧病浔阳城。

By the banks of the Xunyang River, I bid farewell to a friend one night. Maple leaves and reed flowers tremble in the chill of autumn.
I dismount; my guest remains aboard his boat. We raise our wine cups, but there is no music to accompany us.
Though tipsy, joy eludes us as sorrowful parting draws near. At the moment of goodbye, the vast river reflects the moon.
Suddenly, from over the water comes the sound of a pipa. Forgetting home, both host and guest linger on.
Following the notes, I ask softly who plays. The pipa stops; she wishes to speak, yet hesitates.
I move my boat closer and invite her out. We refill the wine, trim the lamp, and resume the banquet.
After countless calls, she finally appears, still holding the pipa half-hiding her face.
She turns the tuning pegs and plucks a few strings. Before the melody completes, emotion arises first.
Each string sighs with suppressed longing, seeming to tell a life of unfulfilled ambition.
Head bowed, fingers moving freely, she continues playing, pouring out infinite tales of her heart.
With gentle pinches, slow twists, sweeps, and picks, she first plays "Rainbow Garments," then "Six Strings."
The thick strings roar like sudden rain; the thin ones whisper like private talk.
Roaring and whispering intertwine, sounding like large and small pearls falling onto a jade plate.
Smooth like oriole song beneath flowers, choked like water struggling under ice.
Cold ice makes the flow stiff, causing the strings to freeze; when they can no longer resonate, sound pauses briefly.
Then new hidden sorrows and deep regrets emerge. In this silence, meaning surpasses any sound.
Like a silver vase suddenly bursting, water spattering forth; like armored cavalry charging, swords and spears clashing.
When the piece ends, she strikes her plectrum centrally across the strings. One final note sounds like tearing silk.
Boats to the east and west fall silent. Only the white autumn moon above the river center is seen.
She sighs, puts away her plectrum between the strings, adjusts her clothes, and composes herself.

Nobles from Five Villages competed to give me silk scarves. For one performance, I received countless bolts.
Jeweled hairpins and silver combs broke keeping time. Blood-red skirts stained by spilled wine.
Year after year in laughter and joy, I casually let moonlit autumns and spring breezes pass.
My brother joined the army; my aunt died. Days and nights fled; my youth faded.
Before my door, visitors grew scarce. Aging, I married a merchant.
The merchant values profit over love. Last month he went to Fuliang to trade tea.
While he is gone, I guard our empty boat at the river mouth. Moonlight circles the ship; river water runs cold.
Deep in the night, I dreamt of youthful days. Waking weeping, rouge tears run down my face.
Hearing her pipa, I already sighed. Hearing these words, I mourn further.
We are both lost souls wandering the ends of the earth. Why must we have known each other before meeting?

Tipsy yet joyless, we part in sorrow,

Making me forget to return home and my guest forget to set sail.

Refill the wine, trim the lamp, and resume the feast.

Still holding her pipa, half-covering her face.

Each string restrains its voice, every note carries longing,
Seeming to recount a lifetime of thwarted ambitions.
Head bowed low, she plays with casual ease,
Expressing all the boundless matters of her heart.

The thin strings whisper like private murmurs.
Roaring and whispering intermingle in complex play,
Like large and small pearls falling onto a jade plate.
Now sweet like orioles singing smoothly beneath flowers,
Now choked like spring water struggling under ice.
When the cold, sticky ice halts the flow, the strings seem frozen,
And this stillness cuts off the sound for a brief pause.
But within that silence arise hidden sorrows and secret resentments—
At this moment, silence speaks louder than sound.

Then suddenly, like a silver vase bursting, water spurts forth,
Or iron cavalry charging, clashing swords and spears ring out.
As the song ends, she draws the plectrum across the center,
All four strings strike one final note, tearing silk apart.

Only the white autumn moon seen in the middle of the river.

Straightens her clothes, rises, and composes her solemn face.

My home was near the Shrimp Mound Hill.
At thirteen, I mastered the pipa,
My name listed first in the Imperial Music Bureau.
My performances impressed even master musicians,
And when made up, my beauty incited the envy of courtesans.
Young nobles from Five Tombs vied to gift me brocade,
For one song, red silk received beyond counting.
Jeweled hairpins snapped keeping time to the rhythm,
Blood-red skirts stained by overturned wine.
Year after year passed in laughter and merriment,
Autumn moons and spring breezes spent idly away.

{"source": {"title": "琵琶行", "author": "白居易", "text": "浔阳江头夜送客，枫叶荻花秋瑟瑟。
主人下马客在船，举酒欲饮无管弦。
醉不成欢惨将别，别时茫茫江浸月。
忽闻水上琵琶声，主人忘归客不发。
寻声暗问弹者谁，琵琶声停欲语迟。
移船相近邀相见，添酒回灯重开宴。
千呼万唤始出来，犹抱琵琶半遮面。
转轴拨弦三两声，未成曲调先有情。
弦弦掩抑声声思，似诉平生不得志。
低眉信手续续弹，说尽心中无限事。
轻拢慢捻抹复挑，初为霓裳后六幺。
大弦嘈嘈如急雨，小弦切切如私语。
嘈嘈切切错杂弹，大珠小珠落玉盘。
间关莺语花底滑，幽咽泉流冰下难。
冰泉冷涩弦凝绝，凝绝不通声暂歇。
别有幽愁暗恨生，此时无声胜有声。
银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。
曲终收拨当心画，四弦一声如裂帛。
东船西舫悄无言，唯见江心秋月白。
沉吟放拨插弦中，整顿衣裳起敛容。
自言本是京城女，家在虾蟆陵下住。
十三学得琵琶成，名属教坊第一部。
曲罢曾教善才服，妆成每被秋娘妒。
五陵年少争缠头，一曲红绡不知数。
钿头银篦击节碎，血色罗裙翻酒污。
今年欢笑复明年，秋月春风等闲度。
弟走从军阿姨死，暮去朝来颜色故。
门前冷落鞍马稀，老大嫁作商人妇。
商人重利轻别离，前月浮梁买茶去。
去来江口守空船，绕船月明江水寒。
夜深忽梦少年事，梦啼妆泪红阑干。
我闻琵琶已叹息，又闻此语重唧唧。
同是天涯沦落人，相逢何必曾相识！
我从去年辞帝京，谪居卧病浔阳城。
浔阳地僻无音乐，终岁不闻丝竹声。
住近湓江地低湿，黄芦苦竹绕宅生。
其间旦暮闻何物？杜鹃啼血猿哀鸣。
春江花朝秋月夜，往往取酒还独倾。
岂无山歌与村笛？呕哑嘲哳难为听。
今夜闻君琵琶语，如听仙乐耳暂明。
莫辞更坐弹一曲，为君翻作琵琶行。
感我此言良久立，却坐促弦弦转急。
凄凄不似向前声，满座重闻皆掩泣。
座中泣下谁最多？江州司马青衫湿。"}, "translation": "**The Song of the Pipa**

By the Xunyang River, at night I saw off a guest;
Maple leaves and reed flowers rustled in chill.
I dismounted, my guest was on his boat;
We raised our cups to drink, but there were no pipes or strings.
Drunk, yet without joy, we faced our sorrowful parting;
When we parted, the vast river soaked in moonlight.
Suddenly, over the water, came the sound of a pipa;
I forgot to return, and my guest delayed his departure.
Following the sound, I asked softly: "Who is playing?"
The pipa stopped, as if she wished to speak but hesitated.
I moved my boat close to invite her out;
Added wine, turned up the lamps, and reopened the feast.
Called thousands of times, summoned ten thousand voices, only then did she appear,
Still holding the pipa, half-hiding her face behind it.
Turning the pegs, plucking the strings for two or three notes,
Before any melody formed, feeling was already there.
Every string hidden, every note full of thought,
As if telling of lifelong frustrations unfulfilled.
Eyes lowered, fingers trusting, she played on continuously,
Voicing all the endless matters within her heart.
Light gathering, slow twisting, wiping, then picking—
First the *Neichang* (Court Dance), then the *Liuyao*.
The thick strings clamored like sudden rain,
The thin strings whispered like private talk.
Clamoring and whispering, mixed together in play,
Large pearls and small pearls falling into a jade plate.
Smooth and sliding like orioles singing beneath flowers,
Choking and sobbing like springs struggling under ice.
Cold ice, sluggish springs, strings froze and cut off;
Frozen, blocked, the sound paused for a moment.
A different kind of hidden sorrow, silent hatred arose;
At this moment, silence surpassed speech.
Suddenly, a silver vase burst, water splashing forth,
Iron cavalry charged, swords and spears clanging.
The tune ended; she drew her pick across the center strings,
Four strings sounded once, sharp as tearing silk.
East boats and west barges fell silent, saying nothing,
Only the white autumn moon on the river’s heart remained visible.
She pondered, put down her pick between the strings,
Straightened her clothes, rose, composing her expression.
She said: "Originally a girl from the capital city,
My home was near Toad Tomb Hill.
At thirteen I mastered the pipa,
My name belonged to the first troupe of the Imperial Music Bureau.
After finishing a song, even master musicians admired me;
Once made up, courtesans like Qiu Niang often envied me.
Young nobles from the Five Tombs vied to gift me scarves,
For one song, red silks numbered beyond count.
Jeweled heads and silver combs snapped keeping rhythm,
Crimson skirts stained by spilled wine.
This year laughter joined next year's delight,
Autumn moons and spring winds passed casually.
My brother went off to war, my aunt died,
Evenings fade, mornings come, beauty fades with time.
Front gate deserted, horses and carriages rare,
Growing old, I married a merchant’s wife.
Merchants value profit, care little for parting,
Last month he went to Fuliang to buy tea.
He left, I stayed at the river mouth guarding an empty boat,
Moonlight encircling the empty boat, river water cold.
Deep in the night, suddenly dreaming of youthful days,
In dreams I cry, makeup tears stain the red railing dry."

I heard the pipa and sighed deeply,
Then hearing these words, I moaned again.
Both are people fallen adrift at sky’s edge,
Meeting here, why must we have known each other before?
I left the imperial capital last year,
Demoted, lying ill in Xunyang City.
Xunyang is remote, devoid of music,
All year long, no pipes or strings are heard.
Living near the Pen River, land low and damp,
Yellow reeds and bitter bamboo grow around my house.
What do I hear here morning and evening?
Cuckoos crying blood, gibbons wailing mournfully.
Spring rivers, flower mornings, autumn moon nights,
Often I take wine and pour it alone.
Are there not mountain songs and village flutes?
Gurgling and noisy, impossible to listen to.
Tonight, hearing your pipa’s language,
It is like hearing immortal music; my ears become momentarily clear.
Do not refuse to sit again and play another piece,
For you, I will rewrite this *Song of the Pipa*.

Moved by my words, she stood for a long while,
Then sat back down, tightening the strings, which grew urgent.
Mournful sounds unlike those before,
Those present listened anew, covering their faces in tears.
Among those seated, who wept most?
The blue robe of the Sima of Jiangzhou was wet."}

无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
